@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Mask:
    """Which entries were hidden, and how they were chosen.

    ``hidden`` is a boolean array the same shape as the counts, true where an
    entry was set to zero. ``scheme`` records how they were picked, because
    the library-size correction is only valid under one of them.
    """

    hidden: np.ndarray
    #: How the hidden entries were chosen. ``"mcar"``, missing completely at
    #: random, is the only scheme built, and the only one
    #: :meth:`library_scale` will answer for.
    scheme: str = MCAR

    @property
    def n_hidden(self) -> int:
        return int(self.hidden.sum())

    @property
    def fraction_hidden(self) -> float:
        return self.n_hidden / self.hidden.size if self.hidden.size else 0.0

    def positions(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """The hidden entries as an array of (sample, gene) pairs."""
        return np.argwhere(self.hidden)

    def visible_per_sample(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """How many of each sample's genes the model was shown, as ``[samples]``."""
        return self.hidden.shape[1] - self.hidden.sum(axis=1)

    def library_scale(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """What a sample's observed total is multiplied by to estimate its true total.

        The number of genes divided by the number of that sample's entries the
        model was shown. A sample with a fifth of its entries hidden has its
        observed total raised by about a quarter, and the exact factor differs
        from sample to sample because the hidden entries are drawn per gene
        rather than per sample.

        Returned as ``[samples, 1]`` so it multiplies a column of row totals
        directly.

        :raises DataError: for any scheme but ``"mcar"``, naming why. The
            estimate stands on the shown entries being a random subsample of
            the sample's, which only missing completely at random guarantees.
        :raises DataError: if any sample has no visible entry at all, since
            nothing is then left to estimate its total from.
        """
        if self.scheme != MCAR:
            raise DataError(
                f"the library-size correction under a mask is only valid for the "
                f"{MCAR!r} scheme and this mask says {self.scheme!r}. The "
                f"correction multiplies a sample's observed total by its genes "
                f"over the entries it was shown, which estimates the true total "
                f"only when the shown entries are a random subsample of the "
                f"sample's. A scheme that hides entries according to their "
                f"values breaks that, and the estimate would be biased rather "
                f"than unavailable."
            )
        n_genes = self.hidden.shape[1]
        visible = self.visible_per_sample()
        if (visible == 0).any():
            empty = int((visible == 0).sum())
            raise DataError(
                f"{empty} sample(s) have every entry hidden, so there is nothing "
                f"left to estimate their total counts from. Hide a smaller "
                f"fraction."
            )
        return (n_genes / visible).astype(np.float32).reshape(-1, 1)

def mcar_mask(
    n_samples: int,
    n_genes: int,
    fraction: float,
    rng: np.random.Generator,
) -> Mask:
    """Choose which entries to hide, the same proportion within every gene.

    :param fraction: the proportion of each gene's samples to hide, between 0
        and 1. The number hidden per gene is rounded down, so a fraction below
        ``1 / n_samples`` hides nothing and says so.
    """
    if not 0.0 <= fraction <= 1.0:
        raise DataError(f"fraction must lie between 0 and 1, got {fraction}")

    hidden = np.zeros((n_samples, n_genes), dtype=bool)
    per_gene = int(fraction * n_samples)
    if per_gene == 0:
        if fraction > 0:
            raise DataError(
                f"a fraction of {fraction} over {n_samples} samples rounds down to "
                f"no hidden entries per gene, so nothing would be masked. Use a "
                f"fraction of at least {1 / n_samples:.3g}, or turn masking off."
            )
        return Mask(hidden=hidden, scheme=MCAR)

    # One independent draw per gene, vectorised. Version 0.1 looped in Python
    # over every gene and called random.sample inside, which on a
    # twenty-thousand gene matrix is twenty thousand calls.
    for gene in range(n_genes):
        chosen = rng.choice(n_samples, size=per_gene, replace=False)
        hidden[chosen, gene] = True

    return Mask(hidden=hidden, scheme=MCAR)

def apply_mask(counts: np.ndarray, mask: Mask) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return a copy of the counts with the hidden entries set to zero."""
    if counts.shape != mask.hidden.shape:
        raise DataError(
            f"the mask is shaped {mask.hidden.shape} but the counts are "
            f"{counts.shape}; they have to match"
        )
    masked = counts.copy()
    masked[mask.hidden] = 0
    return masked

docs.title: preffect.data.batching
docs.text:
Dividing samples into mini-batches.

A mini-batch is the handful of samples the model looks at before it adjusts itself once. Smaller batches mean more adjustments per pass over the data.

Every sample is used. Version 0.1 skipped the final batch of each epoch whenever it was smaller than the requested size, so with 250 samples and a batch of 200, fifty never entered training and nothing said so. On one of the published datasets that was 13 of 123 samples, every epoch. Here the last batch is kept at whatever size it is, and dropping it is something you ask for. That is defect 6 in how_this_project_breaks.md.

def n_batches(n_samples: int, batch_size: int, drop_last: bool = False) -> int:
    """How many batches one pass over the data will produce."""
    if n_samples <= 0:
        return 0
    whole, remainder = divmod(n_samples, batch_size)
    return whole if (drop_last or remainder == 0) else whole + 1

def batch_indices(
    n_samples: int,
    batch_size: int,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
    shuffle: bool = True,
    drop_last: bool = False,
) -> list[np.ndarray]:
    """Divide the sample positions into batches.

    :param rng: required when shuffling, so that a run with a seed is
        repeatable. Version 0.1 shuffled from the global random state, which is
        why its runs could not be reproduced even when a seed was set
        elsewhere.
    :param drop_last: discard a final short batch. Off by default.
    :returns: a list of arrays of positions. With ``drop_last`` off, every
        position from 0 to ``n_samples - 1`` appears exactly once across them.
    """
    if batch_size < 1:
        raise ConfigError(f"batch_size must be at least 1, got {batch_size}")
    if n_samples <= 0:
        return []

    if shuffle:
        if rng is None:
            raise ConfigError(
                "shuffling needs a random number generator, so that a run with a "
                "seed can be repeated. Pass one, or set shuffle=False."
            )
        order = rng.permutation(n_samples)
    else:
        order = np.arange(n_samples)

    if batch_size > n_samples:
        # One batch of everything. Version 0.1 handled this by writing the
        # reduced size back into the shared settings, so the change outlived
        # the call and affected everything built afterwards.
        batch_size = n_samples

    batches = [order[i : i + batch_size] for i in range(0, n_samples, batch_size)]
    if drop_last and len(batches[-1]) < batch_size:
        batches.pop()
    return batches

docs.title: preffect.data.tensors
docs.text:
Turning checked count data into the tensors a model takes.

Keeps two count matrices apart, and the distinction matters:

  • inputs are what the model sees. With masking on, some entries have been set to zero on purpose.
  • targets are what it is scored against, always the original counts.

Version 0.1 kept both as well, under the names Xs and Rs, but chose between them inside the training loop with a test on the task name, so a run could be scored against the wrong one depending on a string.

A third thing travels with a masked split: how much of each sample's total the hiding took away. The model scales everything it predicts for a sample by that sample's total count, and read off the inputs that total is short by the hidden fraction while the targets are not. library_scale is the factor that repairs it, derived from the mask whenever there is one, and finding 56 is what happened without it.

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class TensorData:
    """One split, ready for a model."""

    inputs: torch.Tensor
    targets: torch.Tensor
    corrections: torch.Tensor | None = None
    batch_labels: torch.Tensor | None = None
    mask: Mask | None = None
    #: The sample-sample network as ``[2, edges]``, both directions, or None
    #: for the simple model. An edge list rather than a square matrix because
    #: these networks are very sparse; see data/graph.py.
    edge_index: torch.Tensor | None = None
    #: What each sample's observed total has to be multiplied by to estimate
    #: the total it would have had with nothing hidden, as ``[samples, 1]``.
    #: Filled in from the mask when there is one and left None when there is
    #: not, so a split with nothing hidden is untouched. See
    #: :meth:`~preffect.data.masking.Mask.library_scale` and finding 56.
    library_scale: torch.Tensor | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.inputs.shape != self.targets.shape:
            raise DataError(
                f"inputs are shaped {tuple(self.inputs.shape)} and targets "
                f"{tuple(self.targets.shape)}; they have to match"
            )
        for name in ("corrections", "batch_labels", "library_scale"):
            value = getattr(self, name)
            if value is not None and value.shape[0] != self.inputs.shape[0]:
                raise DataError(
                    f"{name} has {value.shape[0]} rows but there are "
                    f"{self.inputs.shape[0]} samples"
                )
        # Derived here rather than at every call site, so that an experiment
        # which builds its own TensorData with a mask gets the correction
        # without being edited. A scale supplied by hand wins, which is how
        # ``select`` carries one into a batch: a batch has no mask of its own.
        if self.mask is not None and self.library_scale is None:
            scale = torch.from_numpy(self.mask.library_scale()).to(
                device=self.inputs.device, dtype=self.inputs.dtype
            )
            if scale.shape[0] != self.inputs.shape[0]:
                raise DataError(
                    f"the mask covers {scale.shape[0]} samples but there are "
                    f"{self.inputs.shape[0]}"
                )
            object.__setattr__(self, "library_scale", scale)

    @property
    def n_samples(self) -> int:
        return self.inputs.shape[0]

    @property
    def n_genes(self) -> int:
        return self.inputs.shape[1]

    @property
    def has_network(self) -> bool:
        return self.edge_index is not None

    def select(self, positions: np.ndarray | torch.Tensor) -> TensorData:
        """One mini-batch, as a smaller :class:`TensorData`.

        When a network is present the subgraph is induced on the batch, so an
        edge survives only when both endpoints are in it. Most are not; see
        data/graph.py.

        The mask does not come along, because it describes the whole split and
        a batch is a handful of its rows. The library-size correction does, as
        the rows of it this batch covers, which is why it is a field of its own
        rather than something recomputed from the mask.
        """
        # On the data's device. Built on the CPU regardless, as it was until
        # finding 45, the subgraph induction below indexed a CPU table with a
        # CUDA edge_index and the first batch of any graph model on a GPU
        # raised a device mismatch.
        index = torch.as_tensor(positions, dtype=torch.long, device=self.inputs.device)
        return TensorData(
            inputs=self.inputs[index],
            targets=self.targets[index],
            corrections=None if self.corrections is None else self.corrections[index],
            batch_labels=(
                None if self.batch_labels is None else self.batch_labels[index]
            ),
            edge_index=(
                None
                if self.edge_index is None
                else induce_subgraph(self.edge_index, index, self.n_samples)
            ),
            library_scale=(
                None if self.library_scale is None else self.library_scale[index]
            ),
        )

    def adjacency_matrix(self) -> torch.Tensor:
        """The network for these samples as a square 0/1 matrix.

        Built on demand and only for a batch, where it is small. Holding the
        square form for a whole cohort would be 1.6 GB at 20,000 samples and
        almost entirely zeros.
        """
        if self.edge_index is None:
            raise DataError("this split carries no sample-sample network")
        dense = torch.zeros(
            (self.n_samples, self.n_samples),
            dtype=torch.float32,
            device=self.inputs.device,
        )
        if self.edge_index.numel():
            dense[self.edge_index[0], self.edge_index[1]] = 1.0
        return dense

    def to(self, device: str | torch.device) -> TensorData:
        """Return a copy with every tensor moved to ``device``.

        A new object rather than a move in place, because this class is frozen
        and because leaving the caller holding something whose contents have
        silently relocated is how a confusing device error happens three
        functions later.

        The mask is not a tensor and is carried across unchanged: it records
        which entries were hidden, which is a fact about the data rather than
        something the model computes with. The library-size correction derived
        from it is a tensor the model multiplies by, so it moves.
        """
        return TensorData(
            inputs=self.inputs.to(device),
            targets=self.targets.to(device),
            corrections=None if self.corrections is None else self.corrections.to(device),
            batch_labels=(
                None if self.batch_labels is None else self.batch_labels.to(device)
            ),
            mask=self.mask,
            edge_index=None if self.edge_index is None else self.edge_index.to(device),
            library_scale=(
                None if self.library_scale is None else self.library_scale.to(device)
            ),
        )

def encode_corrections(
    adata: ad.AnnData, variables: tuple[CorrectionVariable, ...]
) -> torch.Tensor | None:
    """Pull the correction variables out of the sample annotations.

    Categorical variables become integer codes, continuous ones stay as they
    are. Returns ``None`` when there are no correction variables, so the
    absence is explicit rather than an empty tensor that later code has to
    remember to check.

    :raises DataError: naming any variable the data does not carry, and listing
        what it does carry, since a misspelled column is the usual cause.
    """
    if not variables:
        return None

    missing = [v.name for v in variables if v.name not in adata.obs.columns]
    if missing:
        raise DataError(
            f"correction variable(s) {missing} are not in the sample annotations. "
            f"Available: {sorted(adata.obs.columns)}"
        )

    # Rows padded in for a patient missing this tissue carry no annotations at
    # all, so they are the likely cause of a missing value here and the
    # message says so rather than leaving someone looking at their own file.
    from preffect.data.tissues import ghost_rows

    n_padded = int(ghost_rows(adata).sum())
    padded_note = (
        f" {n_padded} row(s) here were padded in for patients with no sample in "
        f"this tissue, and a padded row carries no annotations, so a run that "
        f"pads cannot also use correction variables."
        if n_padded
        else ""
    )

    columns = []
    for variable in variables:
        values = adata.obs[variable.name]
        if variable.kind == "categorical":
            codes = values.astype("category").cat.codes.to_numpy()
            if (codes < 0).any():
                raise DataError(
                    f"correction variable {variable.name!r} has missing values. "
                    f"Fill them in, or give them a level of their own." + padded_note
                )
            columns.append(codes.astype(np.float32))
        else:
            numeric = values.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
            if np.isnan(numeric).any():
                raise DataError(
                    f"continuous correction variable {variable.name!r} has "
                    f"missing values." + padded_note
                )
            columns.append(numeric.astype(np.float32))

    return torch.from_numpy(np.column_stack(columns))

def to_tensors(
    adata: ad.AnnData,
    correction_variables: tuple[CorrectionVariable, ...] = (),
    mask: Mask | None = None,
    batch_column: str | None = "batch",
    with_network: bool = False,
) -> TensorData:
    """Build the tensors for one split.

    :param mask: entries to hide from the model. The targets keep the original
        values, so the model is scored on what it should have recovered. The
        library-size correction for the hiding is derived from it here, so
        nothing downstream has to remember to ask for it.
    :param batch_column: sample annotation naming each sample's batch, used
        only by the batch centroid term. Ignored when the column is absent.
    :param with_network: read the sample-sample network, which the single and
        full models need. Asking for it when it is absent is an error rather
        than a silent fallback: version 0.1 quietly turned a request for a
        graph model into a plain one, which is finding 2.
    """
    counts = adata.X
    dense = np.asarray(counts.todense()) if hasattr(counts, "todense") else np.asarray(counts)
    targets = torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(dense, dtype=np.float32))

    if mask is None:
        inputs = targets.clone()
    else:
        inputs = torch.from_numpy(
            np.ascontiguousarray(apply_mask(dense, mask), dtype=np.float32)
        )

    batch_labels = None
    if batch_column and batch_column in adata.obs.columns:
        codes = adata.obs[batch_column].astype("category").cat.codes.to_numpy()
        batch_labels = torch.from_numpy(codes.astype(np.int64))

    return TensorData(
        inputs=inputs,
        targets=targets,
        corrections=encode_corrections(adata, correction_variables),
        batch_labels=batch_labels,
        mask=mask,
        edge_index=load_adjacency(adata) if with_network else None,
    )

docs.title: preffect.data.graph
docs.text:
The sample-sample network: reading it, and cutting it down to a mini-batch.

The graph models attach a network saying which samples resemble each other. It is stored in the count file under obsm['sample_sample_adj'] as a square matrix, one row and column per sample, with a one where two samples are linked.

docs.title: Edges are kept as a list, not a square matrix
docs.text: A square matrix of 20,000 samples is 1.6 GB and almost entirely zeros: these networks have three or four neighbours per sample. The edge list is a few hundred kilobytes. The square form is rebuilt only for the handful of samples in a mini-batch, where it is small.

docs.title: Most edges do not survive a mini-batch, and that is reported
docs.text:
An edge is usable only when both of its endpoints are in the same batch, and the share that survives is the batch size divided by the sample count. On a cohort of a few thousand that is a small fraction; on this project's real datasets, which run from 48 to 528 samples, it is between 38% and all of them. Version 0.1 did the same thing silently either way. Here :func:edge_survival measures it so a run can say so.

Finding 22 in how_this_project_breaks.md; whether to batch the graph properly instead is issue #12.

def has_adjacency(adata: ad.AnnData) -> bool:

    Every one of the nine datasets version 0.1 shipped carries an identity
    matrix, which is an entry with every sample linked to itself and nothing
    else, and :func:`load_adjacency` drops self-links, so the edge list comes
    back empty. This returns True for all of them. Finding 35, which is how
    that was discovered for eight of them: a graph model trained for hours over
    a graph with no edges, and the loss fell the whole time. Finding 54 found
    the ninth was the same identity with its rows subset, and why: a bug in

def load_adjacency(adata: ad.AnnData, split: str = "data") -> torch.Tensor:
    """Read the network as an edge list of shape ``[2, edges]``.

    Both directions of every edge are included, which is what a graph attention
    layer expects. Self-links are dropped: every sample attends to itself
    anyway, and counting them would flatter any measure of how well the network
    is reconstructed.

    :raises DataError: if the network is missing or not square.
    """
    if not has_adjacency(adata):
        raise DataError(
            f"{split} has no sample-sample network under obsm[{ADJACENCY_KEY!r}], "
            f"which the single and full models need. Use the simple model, or "
            f"add one. Present: {sorted(adata.obsm) or '(nothing)'}"
        )

    matrix = adata.obsm[ADJACENCY_KEY]
    dense = np.asarray(matrix.todense()) if hasattr(matrix, "todense") else np.asarray(matrix)

    n = adata.n_obs
    if dense.shape != (n, n):
        raise DataError(
            f"{split}'s network is shaped {dense.shape} but there are {n} samples; "
            f"it has to be square with one row per sample"
        )

    dense = np.array(dense)
    self_links = int(np.count_nonzero(np.diag(dense)))
    np.fill_diagonal(dense, 0)
    rows, cols = np.nonzero(dense)

    if rows.size == 0:
        raise DataError(
            f"{split}'s sample-sample network has no edges between different "
            f"samples"
            + (f" (only {self_links} self-links)" if self_links else "")
            + f". A graph model over {n} unconnected samples has nothing to "
            f"attend to: it costs about ten times the parameters and twenty "
            f"times the time of the simple model and cannot use any of it. "
            f"Use the simple model, or supply a network with real edges. "
            f"Every dataset version 0.1 shipped carries an identity matrix "
            f"here, so this is the common case, not a rare one. See findings "
            f"35 and 54."
        )

    return torch.from_numpy(np.vstack([rows, cols]).astype(np.int64))

def induce_subgraph(
    edge_index: torch.Tensor, positions: torch.Tensor, n_total: int
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Keep the edges whose endpoints are both in this batch, renumbered locally.

    :param positions: the samples in the batch, as positions into the whole
        split.
    :returns: ``[2, kept]`` with indices in ``0 .. len(positions) - 1``, ready
        for a graph layer that knows nothing about the samples left out.
    """
    # Everything on edge_index's device. The table and the positions were
    # built on the CPU whatever the edges' device, which no CPU run could
    # notice and every GPU run fell over on. Finding 45.
    device = edge_index.device
    positions = torch.as_tensor(positions, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    local = torch.full((n_total,), -1, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    local[positions] = torch.arange(len(positions), device=device)

    both_present = (local[edge_index[0]] >= 0) & (local[edge_index[1]] >= 0)
    kept = edge_index[:, both_present]
    return torch.stack([local[kept[0]], local[kept[1]]])

def edge_survival(
    edge_index: torch.Tensor,
    batches: list[np.ndarray] | list[torch.Tensor],
    n_total: int,
) -> EdgeSurvival:
    """Count how many edges survive a particular division into batches.

    Counts each undirected edge once, so the number matches what a person would
    get by counting lines in the network.
    """
    undirected = edge_index[:, edge_index[0] < edge_index[1]]
    total = undirected.shape[1]

    kept = sum(
        induce_subgraph(undirected, torch.as_tensor(positions), n_total).shape[1]
        for positions in batches
    )
    sizes = [len(b) for b in batches]
    return EdgeSurvival(
        total_edges=total,
        kept_edges=kept,
        n_samples=n_total,
        batch_size=max(sizes) if sizes else 0,
    )

docs.title: preffect.data.tissues
docs.text:
Matching samples across tissues, for the full model.

The full model takes several profiles from the same patient, for example a tumour and the normal tissue beside it, and uses them together. To do that it has to know which row of one file corresponds to which row of another.

The files do not share sample names, deliberately. In the project's own data the names are tau1_0 and tau2_0, so a join on names would match nothing. The correspondence is written down instead, in a table under obsm['sample_association'] with one column per tissue, giving each sample's counterpart in every other tissue. A patient with no counterpart in some tissue has an empty cell in that tissue's column.

docs.title: A patient missing a tissue is padded, not refused
docs.text:
A cohort where some patients lack a matched normal is the common case in practice, and until 2026-11-02 version 0.2 refused one outright. It now does what version 0.1 did, ported rule for rule and then measured:

  • Every empty cell becomes a row of its own in that tissue, called a ghost row here and in version 0.1. It gets a name of its own, every annotation missing, and its counts set to the rounded per-gene mean of that tissue's real samples.
  • The tissue's network is enlarged to cover the ghost rows, with no links, so a ghost attends to nothing and nothing attends to it.
  • Ghost rows are left out of the expression reconstruction term, the two library-size terms and the imputation scores, and kept in the latent and network terms. That split is version 0.1's, made in code rather than stated: it commented out the lines that would have removed ghosts from the latent and network parameters. The decision record of 2026-11-02 names it as inherited and measures it.
  • Hidden entries are never drawn from a ghost row, which :class:MultiTissueData refuses rather than trusts.

align_tissues(..., unmatched="refuse") brings the old refusal back. That is not a historical courtesy: dropping the patients who are missing a tissue is the real alternative to padding, and it is the arm the measurement in exp/19_unmatched_samples_padded compares padding against.

docs.title: What a ghost row cannot carry
docs.text: Its annotations are all missing, by the rule above, so a padded run has no correction variable and no batch label for it. Correction variables are refused by name when any value is missing (:func:~preffect.data.tensors.encode_corrections), which means a padded run and correction variables cannot be combined today. Fill the annotations in yourself, or drop the incomplete patients, or leave the correction variables out.

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class TissueAlignment:
    """Tissues whose rows line up, and which of those rows are padding.

    Returned rather than a bare list so that the padding is handed back as a
    value, not only written into the tissues. The two say the same thing:
    ``ghosts[i]`` is :func:`ghost_rows` of ``tissues[i]``.
    """

    tissues: list[ad.AnnData]

        return [int(g.sum()) for g in self.ghosts]

    def any_ghosts(self) -> bool:
        return any(bool(g.any()) for g in self.ghosts)

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class MultiTissueData:
    """Several tissues whose rows refer to the same patients, in the same order.

    ``tissues[0]`` is the target: the profile the full model predicts. The rest
    inform that prediction without being predicted themselves, which is what
    version 0.1 does and what the paper describes as stabilising a profile
    using matched tissues.

    ``ghosts`` records which rows were padded in for a patient missing that
    tissue, one boolean tensor per tissue. Leave it unset when the cohort is
    complete: the terms that leave ghost rows out are then skipped entirely
    rather than given an all-true selection, so a complete cohort trains bit
    for bit as it did before padding existed.
    """

    tissues: list[TensorData]
    #: One ``[samples]`` boolean tensor per tissue, True where the row is
    #: padding. None when no tissue has any, which is the ordinary case.
    ghosts: list[torch.Tensor] | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not self.tissues:
            raise DataError("a multi-tissue dataset needs at least one tissue")
        sizes = {t.n_samples for t in self.tissues}
        if len(sizes) > 1:
            raise DataError(
                f"the tissues have different sample counts {sorted(sizes)}; they "
                f"must be aligned first"
            )
        genes = {t.n_genes for t in self.tissues}
        if len(genes) > 1:
            raise DataError(f"the tissues have different gene counts {sorted(genes)}")

        if self.ghosts is None:
            return
        if len(self.ghosts) != len(self.tissues):
            raise DataError(
                f"there are {len(self.tissues)} tissue(s) but {len(self.ghosts)} "
                f"record(s) of which rows are padding; there must be one per tissue"
            )
        for index, (tissue, ghost) in enumerate(
            zip(self.tissues, self.ghosts, strict=True), start=1
        ):
            if ghost.dtype is not torch.bool or ghost.dim() != 1:
                raise DataError(
                    f"tissue {index}'s record of padded rows is {ghost.dtype} of "
                    f"shape {tuple(ghost.shape)}; it has to be one boolean per row"
                )
            if ghost.shape[0] != tissue.n_samples:
                raise DataError(
                    f"tissue {index} has {tissue.n_samples} rows but its record of "
                    f"padded rows covers {ghost.shape[0]}"
                )
            self._refuse_hidden_ghosts(index, tissue, ghost)

    @staticmethod
    def _refuse_hidden_ghosts(index: int, tissue: TensorData, ghost: torch.Tensor) -> None:
        """A hidden entry in a padded row would score the model on a value nobody measured.

        A ghost row's counts are the per-gene mean of the real samples, so
        hiding one of them and asking the model to recover it scores it against
        something this package made up. Version 0.1 kept ghost rows out of the
        masked-entry bookkeeping in its batch iterator; this refuses the mask
        instead, because a mask that hides a ghost entry was built wrongly and
        quietly dropping those entries would leave the caller's count of hidden
        entries disagreeing with what was scored.
        """
        if tissue.mask is None or not bool(ghost.any()):
            return
        rows = ghost.detach().cpu().numpy()
        hidden_in_ghosts = int(tissue.mask.hidden[rows].sum())
        if hidden_in_ghosts:
            where = "the target tissue" if index == 1 else f"tissue {index}"
            raise DataError(
                f"the mask for {where} hides {hidden_in_ghosts} entr(ies) in rows "
                f"that were padded in for patients missing that tissue. Those "
                f"counts are the per-gene mean of the real samples, so recovering "
                f"them measures nothing. Build the mask over the real rows and "
                f"leave the padded ones visible."
            )

    @property
    def n_tissues(self) -> int:
        return len(self.tissues)

    @property
    def n_samples(self) -> int:
        return self.tissues[0].n_samples

    @property
    def n_genes(self) -> int:
        return self.tissues[0].n_genes

    @property
    def target(self) -> TensorData:
        """The tissue whose counts the model predicts."""
        return self.tissues[0]

    @property
    def n_ghosts(self) -> list[int]:
        """How many rows of each tissue are padding."""
        if self.ghosts is None:
            return [0] * self.n_tissues
        return [int(g.sum()) for g in self.ghosts]

    def target_real_rows(self) -> torch.Tensor | None:
        """Which rows of the target tissue are real samples, or None if all are.

        None rather than an all-true tensor on purpose. The objective skips the
        selection entirely when this is None, so a cohort with nothing padded
        gives the same numbers to the last bit as it did before padding
        existed.
        """
        if self.ghosts is None or not bool(self.ghosts[0].any()):
            return None
        return ~self.ghosts[0]

    def select(self, positions: np.ndarray | torch.Tensor) -> MultiTissueData:
        """One mini-batch, taken from every tissue at the same positions.

        The same positions in every tissue, which is only meaningful because
        the rows were aligned first. The record of which rows are padding is
        taken at the same positions, so a batch knows which of its own rows
        are padding without having to look back at the whole split.
        """
        tissues = [t.select(positions) for t in self.tissues]
        if self.ghosts is None:
            return MultiTissueData(tissues)
        ghosts = [
            g[torch.as_tensor(positions, dtype=torch.long, device=g.device)]
            for g in self.ghosts
        ]
        return MultiTissueData(tissues, ghosts=ghosts)

    def to(self, device: str | torch.device) -> MultiTissueData:
        """Return a copy with every tissue's tensors moved to ``device``.

        Every tissue goes to the same device. The full model's terms are
        summed across tissues, so a split set would fail at the first sum, and
        failing here with a clear message beats failing there with an obscure
        one. The record of which rows are padding moves too: it selects rows of
        tensors that have moved.
        """
        return MultiTissueData(
            [t.to(device) for t in self.tissues],
            ghosts=None if self.ghosts is None else [g.to(device) for g in self.ghosts],
        )

def unmatched_counts(adatas: list[ad.AnnData], split: str = "data") -> dict[str, int]:
    """How many patients have no sample in each tissue.

    What ``preffect check`` reports, and what decides whether padding has
    anything to do. An empty dictionary when there is only one tissue, or when
    the first tissue carries no correspondence table, since neither case has a
    count to give.
    """
    if len(adatas) < 2 or ASSOCIATION_KEY not in adatas[0].obsm:
        return {}
    expected = [f"tau_{i}" for i in range(1, len(adatas) + 1)]
    table = _combined_table(adatas, expected, split)
    return {c: int(table[c].isna().sum()) for c in expected}

def ghost_profile(counts: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """The counts a padded row carries: the rounded per-gene mean of the real samples.

    Version 0.1's rule, read from its code rather than its comment, which says
    the row is zero "unless ave_ghost_expr is true" and names a setting that
    does not exist. Genes that are missing in every sample average to nothing
    and are filled with zero, as version 0.1 did.
    """
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
        mean = np.nanmean(counts, axis=0) if counts.shape[0] else np.zeros(counts.shape[1])
    return np.round(np.nan_to_num(mean)).astype(np.float32)

def align_tissues(
    adatas: list[ad.AnnData],
    split: str = "data",
    unmatched: str = "pad",
) -> TissueAlignment:
    """Reorder every tissue so row *i* is the same patient throughout.

    Uses the correspondence table, combined across the tissues that carry it so
    that a patient missing the first tissue is still seen, and takes its row
    order as the order for all of them.

    :param unmatched: what to do about a patient with no sample in some tissue.
        ``"pad"``, the default, gives that tissue a row of its own for the
        patient, as described in this module's documentation. ``"refuse"``
        raises instead, which is what version 0.2 did until 2026-11-02 and
        what the caller wants in order to drop the incomplete patients and
        work with a complete cohort.
    :returns: the aligned tissues and, beside them, which of each tissue's rows
        are padding.
    :raises DataError: if the table is missing, names a tissue that is not
        there, does not name this tissue's samples once each, or leaves a
        patient unmatched while ``unmatched="refuse"``.
    """
    if unmatched not in ("pad", "refuse"):
        raise DataError(
            f"unmatched must be 'pad' or 'refuse', got {unmatched!r}. 'pad' gives "
            f"a patient missing a tissue a row of its own there; 'refuse' stops, "
            f"so the caller can drop the incomplete patients."
        )
    if len(adatas) < 2:
        return TissueAlignment(
            tissues=list(adatas),
            ghosts=[np.zeros(a.n_obs, dtype=bool) for a in adatas],
        )

    expected = [f"tau_{i}" for i in range(1, len(adatas) + 1)]
    table = _combined_table(adatas, expected, split)

    counts = {c: int(table[c].isna().sum()) for c in expected}
    if unmatched == "refuse" and any(counts.values()):
        raise DataError(
            f"{split} has samples with no counterpart in every tissue {counts}, "
            f"and this call asked for them to be refused. Drop the incomplete "
            f"patients, use the single model on one tissue, or leave the "
            f"default in place, which pads them."
        )

    taken = {str(n) for a in adatas for n in a.obs_names}
    taken |= {str(v) for c in expected for v in table[c] if not pd.isna(v)}

    plans: list[tuple[ad.AnnData, list[str], np.ndarray]] = []
    ghosts: list[np.ndarray] = []
    filled = table.copy()
    for index, (adata, column) in enumerate(zip(adatas, expected, strict=True), start=1):
        ghost = filled[column].isna().to_numpy()
        names = [str(v) for v in filled[column]]
        if ghost.any():
            fresh = _ghost_names(column, int(ghost.sum()), taken, split)
            taken |= set(fresh)
            for position, name in zip(np.flatnonzero(ghost), fresh, strict=True):
                names[position] = name
        filled[column] = names
        _check_column(column, [n for n, g in zip(names, ghost, strict=True) if not g],
                      adata, index, split)
        ghosts.append(ghost)
        plans.append((adata, names, ghost))

    # Built in a second pass so that every column of the table carries its
    # padded names before any tissue stores a copy of it.
    tissues = [_pad_tissue(adata, names, ghost, filled) for adata, names, ghost in plans]
    return TissueAlignment(tissues=tissues, ghosts=ghosts)

docs.title: preffect.example_data
docs.text:
A small simulated cohort to try PREFFECT on, written by preffect example-data.

Three splits with no sample in common, for each of the three models: the simple model, the single model (the same counts plus a sample-sample network with real edges in it) and the full model (two tissues per patient, under different names, with the correspondence written down). About two seconds, 200 genes, three groups of samples that each raise a different block of genes, so there is something real to find and you can tell whether the model found it. The counts are negative binomial, which is what PREFFECT models.

The genes are drawn once per cohort and shared by its three splits. Each gene has one base level and one dispersion, and every split of that cohort is drawn from them, so the gene that is highly expressed in the training data is the same gene that is highly expressed in the test data. Until finding 65 the draw happened inside :func:simulate, which is called once per split, so the three splits were three unrelated gene populations sharing a set of names: a model fitted on the training split could not track the test split, and the validation loss sat far above the training loss for that reason rather than for any reason about PREFFECT.

Version 0.1's vignettes ship a test/ folder byte-identical to validation/, in all three of simple, single and full, and a published figure shows a user pointing inference at that folder while the caption calls it a held-out test set. The data here is generated rather than committed, for two reasons: counts do not belong in a git repository, and a generator can promise what a committed file cannot. The three splits are drawn from disjoint samples by construction, and :func:write_example_data checks that and raises rather than write them if they are not. Issue #11.

Every file carries the true expected count of every entry, in layers['true_expected_counts']: the negative binomial mean each count was drawn from, before the draw added its noise. Nothing in PREFFECT reads it, and no real cohort can have it. It is there so that an example which fills in hidden entries can be scored against what the entry should have been rather than against one noisy draw of it, and so that a reader can tell at a glance that the file is simulated. preffect check says so when it finds it.

Batch B's genes are really raised. The files have always carried a batch column, and until finding 65 it labelled samples that were drawn identically, so no correction could change anything. Now a fixed share of the genes, drawn once with the rest of the population and so the same genes in every split, are multiplied by :data:BATCH_LIFT in every batch-B sample. It is deliberately smaller than the groups' four-fold lift, so the groups still dominate and the batch is the second thing you see. What it demonstrates is the correction variables, which take a known nuisance label out of the encoder's input, and the interface's batch figure. It does not exercise the objective's batch-centroid term, which training never reaches because no batch labels are passed to it. Which genes moved, and by how much, is written into each file under uns['batch_shifted_genes'] and uns['batch_lift'], so a reader checking whether a correction took the batch out knows where to look.

The full model's two files per split deliberately do not share sample names, as the project's own data does not, so the correspondence goes in a table under obsm['sample_association'] with one column per tissue, which is where :func:preffect.data.tissues.align_tissues looks. unmatched takes the second tissue away from a share of patients, which is the shape of a real cohort where some patients have no matched normal, and is what the full model's padding exists for. It is zero by default and draws no random numbers when it is zero.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GenePopulation:
    """The genes a cohort is drawn from, drawn once and shared by its splits.

    One of these describes a set of genes: what each is expressed at, how
    noisy each is, and which of them batch B raises. Every split of a cohort
    is drawn from the same one, which is what makes a model fitted on the
    training split able to track the test split. Finding 65.
    """

    #: Each gene's mean count before groups, sequencing depth and batch.
    base: np.ndarray
    #: Each gene's negative binomial dispersion. Smaller is noisier.
    dispersion: np.ndarray
    #: Which genes batch B raises, as column numbers.
    batch_genes: np.ndarray
    #: How much batch B raises them.
    batch_lift: float

    @property
    def n_genes(self) -> int:
        """How many genes this population describes."""
        return int(self.base.shape[0])

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ExampleData:
    """What :func:`write_example_data` wrote, and the summary it prints."""

    #: The folder everything was written under.
    out: Path
    #: By model kind, then split: the first tissue's file.
    files: dict[str, dict[str, Path]]
    #: By split: how many patients had their second tissue taken away.
    unmatched: dict[str, int]

    def digest(self, kind: str, split: str) -> str:
        """The first eight hex digits of the md5 of one written file.

        :param kind: ``simple``, ``single`` or ``full``.
        :param split: ``train``, ``validation`` or ``test``.
        """
        return hashlib.md5(self.files[kind][split].read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:8]

    def describe(self) -> str:
        """The lines ``preffect example-data`` prints after writing."""
        lines = [f"wrote {self.out}"]
        for kind in KINDS:
            lines.append(f"  {kind}:")
            for split, n in N_SAMPLES.items():
                tissues = "  2 tissues" if kind == "full" else ""
                lines.append(
                    f"    {split:<11} {n:>3} samples  md5 {self.digest(kind, split)}{tissues}"
                )
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(f"{N_GENES} genes, {N_SUBTYPES} groups, negative binomial counts.")
        lines.append("No sample appears in more than one split, and the three files differ.")
        lines.append(
            "The genes are drawn once per cohort, so every split is the same genes."
        )
        lines.append(
            f"Batch {SHIFTED_BATCH} has {N_BATCH_GENES} of the {N_GENES} genes raised "
            f"{BATCH_LIFT} times, for the correction variables to take out."
        )
        lines.append(
            f"Every file carries the count each entry was drawn from in "
            f"layers['{TRUTH_LAYER}']."
        )
        if any(self.unmatched.values()):
            missing = ", ".join(f"{s} {c}" for s, c in self.unmatched.items())
            lines.append(
                f"The full model's second tissue is missing for some patients "
                f"({missing}); the full model pads a row of per-gene means in for "
                f"each of them."
            )
        else:
            lines.append(
                "The full model's two tissues are the same patients under different names."
            )
        return "\n".join(lines)

def draw_population(
    n_genes: int,
    rng: np.random.Generator,
    *,
    batch_lift: float = BATCH_LIFT,
    batch_share: float = BATCH_SHARE,
) -> GenePopulation:
    """Draw a set of genes for one cohort: levels, dispersions and the batch's genes.

    :param n_genes: how many genes to describe.
    :param rng: the generator; every draw comes from it, so a seed fixes the
        population and so the files.
    :param batch_lift: how much batch B raises its genes.
    :param batch_share: what share of the genes batch B raises, chosen at
        random from all of them, so some fall inside a group's block and some
        outside. A share rather than a count, so it means the same thing at
        any number of genes.
    :raises ConfigError: if the share is not above 0 and at most 1, if it
        rounds down to no genes at all, or if the lift is not positive.
    :returns: the population, to hand to :func:`simulate` once per split.
    """
    if not 0 < batch_share <= 1:
        raise ConfigError(
            f"the share of genes the batch raises has to be above 0 and at most "
            f"1, got {batch_share}"
        )
    n_batch_genes = round(batch_share * n_genes)
    if n_batch_genes == 0:
        raise ConfigError(
            f"a share of {batch_share} over {n_genes} genes rounds down to no "
            f"genes at all, so the batch would change nothing. Use a share of at "
            f"least {0.5 / n_genes:.3g}."
        )
    if batch_lift <= 0:
        raise ConfigError(
            f"the batch lift multiplies counts, so it has to be above 0, got {batch_lift}"
        )
    base = rng.lognormal(mean=3.0, sigma=1.0, size=n_genes)
    dispersion = rng.uniform(2.0, 8.0, size=n_genes)
    batch_genes = np.sort(rng.choice(n_genes, size=n_batch_genes, replace=False))
    return GenePopulation(
        base=base, dispersion=dispersion, batch_genes=batch_genes, batch_lift=float(batch_lift)
    )

def simulate(
    n_samples: int,
    n_genes: int,
    rng: np.random.Generator,
    offset: int,
    groups: np.ndarray | None = None,
    lift: float = 4.0,
    population: GenePopulation | None = None,
    batches: list[str] | np.ndarray | None = None,
):
    """Counts with a subtype signal in them, so an example has something to find.

    Each sample belongs to one of three groups, and each group raises a
    different block of genes. Negative binomial, which is what PREFFECT models,
    so the example is not quietly fitting Gaussian data.

    **Called without a population this draws exactly what it always drew.**
    ``exp/08``, ``exp/11``, ``exp/17`` and ``exp/19`` each call it once for
    their synthetic cohorts and their recorded results depend on the draws, so
    the genes are still drawn inside, in the same order, when none are given.
    ``tests/test_example_data.py`` holds a digest of the result and fails if
    any of that moves.

    :param n_samples: rows to draw.
    :param n_genes: columns to draw.
    :param rng: the generator; every draw comes from it, so a seed fixes the file.
    :param offset: where sample numbering starts, so no name repeats across splits.
    :param groups: the group each sample belongs to. Drawn here when left
        unset; passed in for the full model's second tissue, which is the same
        patients and so must carry the same groups.
    :param lift: how much a group raises its own block of genes. Lower for a
        second tissue, which stands for the quieter normal tissue beside a
        tumour and should not simply repeat the first.
    :param population: the genes to draw from, from :func:`draw_population`.
        Left unset the genes are drawn here, which gives this split its own
        unrelated set of them: fine for a cohort that is one split, wrong for
        a cohort that is several, which is finding 65.
    :param batches: which batch each sample is in. Left unset there is no
        batch effect in the counts. Needs a population, which is what says
        which genes the batch raises.
    :raises DataError: if the population describes a different number of genes,
        or there is not one batch label per sample.
    :raises ConfigError: if batches are given without a population.
    :returns: the counts, the group of each sample, and the sample names.
    """
    drawn = _draw_split(
        n_samples, n_genes, rng, offset, groups=groups, lift=lift,
        population=population, batches=batches,
    )
    return drawn.counts, drawn.groups, drawn.names

def ring_network(n: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """A sample-sample network with real edges, for the single-model example.

    Not an identity matrix. Every real dataset version 0.1 shipped carries one
    of those, which is a network with nothing in it, and a graph model on it
    has nothing to attend to. Findings 35 and 54.

    :param n: samples; each is linked to its neighbours one and five places on.
    :returns: a symmetric ``n`` by ``n`` matrix of zeros and ones.
    """
    network = np.zeros((n, n), dtype=np.int64)
    for i in range(n):
        network[i, (i + 1) % n] = network[(i + 1) % n, i] = 1
        network[i, (i + 5) % n] = network[(i + 5) % n, i] = 1
    return network

def write_example_data(out: Path, *, seed: int = 0, unmatched: float = 0.0) -> ExampleData:
    """Write the example cohort under ``out`` and check the splits are distinct.

    Writes ``<out>/{simple,single}/{train,validation,test}/counts.tau_1.h5ad``
    and, for the full model, two tissues per split,
    ``<out>/full/{train,validation,test}/counts.tau_{1,2}.h5ad``. The same seed
    writes the same files.

    The genes are drawn once per model kind, and the full model's second tissue
    gets its own draw, so within a kind the three splits are the same genes and
    a model fitted on one can be applied to another. Finding 65.

    :param out: the folder to write under; created if missing.
    :param seed: seed for every draw.
    :param unmatched: the share of patients whose second tissue is left out of
        the full model's data, at least 0 and below 1. The first tissue is never
        thinned, because it is the one the model predicts.
    :raises ConfigError: if ``unmatched`` is outside its range.
    :raises DataError: if any two splits share a sample or are the same file,
        which is the promise this exists to keep.
    :returns: what was written.
    """
    import anndata as ad
    import pandas as pd

    if not 0.0 <= unmatched < 1.0:
        raise ConfigError(f"unmatched must be at least 0 and below 1, got {unmatched}")

    out = Path(out)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    offset = 0
    written: dict[str, dict[str, Path]] = {}
    sample_names: dict[str, list[str]] = {}

    for kind in ("simple", "single"):
        # One draw of the genes for this kind's three splits. Drawing it per
        # split, which is what happened until finding 65, made train,
        # validation and test three unrelated cohorts sharing a set of names.
        population = draw_population(N_GENES, rng)
        written[kind] = {}
        for split, n in N_SAMPLES.items():
            batches = batch_labels(n)
            drawn = _draw_split(
                n, N_GENES, rng, offset, population=population, batches=batches
            )
            offset = _advance(offset, n)  # so no sample name is ever reused across splits

            adata = ad.AnnData(drawn.counts)
            # Object dtype, as the package writes names: under pandas 3 a list
            # becomes a string array that anndata 0.11 refuses to write, and a
            # fresh install can resolve exactly that pairing. Finding 48.
            adata.obs_names = pd.Index(drawn.names, dtype=object)
            adata.var_names = pd.Index([f"GENE_{j:04d}" for j in range(N_GENES)], dtype=object)
            adata.obs["subtype"] = pd.Categorical([f"group_{g}" for g in drawn.groups])
            adata.obs["batch"] = pd.Categorical(batches)
            adata.layers[TRUTH_LAYER] = drawn.expected
            _record_the_batch(adata, population, list(adata.var_names))
            if kind == "single":
                adata.obsm["sample_sample_adj"] = ring_network(n)

            folder = out / kind / split
            folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            # The loader looks for '*tau_<n>.h5ad', where n is the tissue
            # number. An example with one tissue is tau_1.
            path = folder / "counts.tau_1.h5ad"
            adata.write_h5ad(path)
            written[kind][split] = path
            sample_names[f"{kind}/{split}"] = drawn.names

    # The full model: two tissues per split, the same patients in each, and a
    # table saying which row of one is which row of the other. Written after
    # the others so the sample names carry on rather than repeating theirs.
    # One draw of the genes per tissue: the two tissues are different tissues,
    # so they are different genes, but every split of a tissue is the same
    # genes as the other splits of that tissue.
    written["full"] = {}
    tissue_populations = [draw_population(N_GENES, rng), draw_population(N_GENES, rng)]
    full_tissue_files: dict[str, list[Path]] = {}
    unmatched_written: dict[str, int] = {}
    for split, n in N_SAMPLES.items():
        # One batch per patient, used for both of that patient's tissues: a
        # batch is a property of when the patient was processed, so it cannot
        # differ between their two samples.
        batches = np.array(batch_labels(n))
        first = _draw_split(
            n, N_GENES, rng, offset, population=tissue_populations[0], batches=batches
        )
        offset = _advance(offset, n)
        # The same patients, so the same groups; a weaker block lift, so the
        # second tissue informs the first rather than repeating it.
        second = _draw_split(
            n, N_GENES, rng, offset, groups=first.groups, lift=1.8,
            population=tissue_populations[1], batches=batches,
        )
        offset = _advance(offset, n)

        # Which patients keep their second tissue. Every one of them unless
        # asked otherwise, and the draw is skipped entirely at zero so that the
        # generator's stream, and so every file, is untouched.
        kept = [np.ones(n, dtype=bool), np.ones(n, dtype=bool)]
        n_drop = int(round(unmatched * n))
        if n_drop:
            kept[1][rng.choice(n, size=n_drop, replace=False)] = False
        unmatched_written[split] = int((~kept[1]).sum())

        # One column per tissue, each listing that tissue's name for the
        # patient on this row. The two tissues share no sample name, as the
        # project's own data does not, so this table is the only link. A
        # patient whose second tissue was taken away has an empty cell there,
        # which is how a real cohort records a missing matched normal.
        association = pd.DataFrame({"tau_1": first.names, "tau_2": second.names})
        # The empty cell is written as the string "NA", which version 0.1 used
        # and which the reader turns into a missing value, rather than as NaN:
        # under pandas 2 a column of names with a float NaN in it is an object
        # column that anndata refuses to write ("non-string objects"), while
        # pandas 3 makes it a string column and writes it. Continuous integration
        # on Python 3.11 resolved pandas 2 and failed on exactly this line.
        association.loc[~kept[1], "tau_2"] = "NA"

        folder = out / "full" / split
        folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        paths = []
        written_names = []
        for tissue, (drawn, rows, population) in enumerate(
            (
                (first, kept[0], tissue_populations[0]),
                (second, kept[1], tissue_populations[1]),
            ),
            start=1,
        ):
            own_names = [name for name, keep in zip(drawn.names, rows, strict=True) if keep]
            own_groups = drawn.groups[rows]
            m = len(own_names)
            adata = ad.AnnData(drawn.counts if rows.all() else drawn.counts[rows])
            adata.obs_names = pd.Index(own_names, dtype=object)
            adata.var_names = pd.Index([f"GENE_{j:04d}" for j in range(N_GENES)], dtype=object)
            adata.obs["subtype"] = pd.Categorical([f"group_{g}" for g in own_groups])
            adata.obs["batch"] = pd.Categorical(list(batches[rows]))
            adata.layers[TRUTH_LAYER] = (
                drawn.expected if rows.all() else drawn.expected[rows]
            )
            _record_the_batch(adata, population, list(adata.var_names))
            adata.obsm["sample_sample_adj"] = ring_network(m)
            # An obsm frame is aligned by index, so each tissue carries the
            # table under its own names, holding the rows for the patients it
            # actually has. On a complete cohort that is the whole table in
            # both files.
            own = association[rows].copy()
            own.index = pd.Index(own_names, dtype=object)
            adata.obsm["sample_association"] = own
            path = folder / f"counts.tau_{tissue}.h5ad"
            adata.write_h5ad(path)
            paths.append(path)
            written_names.extend(own_names)

        full_tissue_files[split] = paths
        written["full"][split] = paths[0]
        sample_names[f"full/{split}"] = written_names

    # The promise this exists to keep. Checked before reporting success,
    # because version 0.1's vignettes failed exactly here and nothing noticed.
    problems = []
    for kind in KINDS:
        splits = list(N_SAMPLES)
        for i, a in enumerate(splits):
            for b in splits[i + 1 :]:
                shared = set(sample_names[f"{kind}/{a}"]) & set(sample_names[f"{kind}/{b}"])
                if shared:
                    problems.append(f"{kind}: {a} and {b} share {len(shared)} sample(s)")
                digest_a = hashlib.md5(written[kind][a].read_bytes()).hexdigest()
                digest_b = hashlib.md5(written[kind][b].read_bytes()).hexdigest()
                if digest_a == digest_b:
                    problems.append(f"{kind}: {a} and {b} are the same file")
    # The second tissue has to differ from the first as well, or the full
    # model would be combining a profile with a copy of itself.
    for split, paths in full_tissue_files.items():
        digests = [hashlib.md5(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in paths]
        if len(set(digests)) != len(digests):
            problems.append(f"full: {split}'s two tissues are the same file")

    if problems:
        raise DataError("the splits are not distinct: " + "; ".join(problems))

    return ExampleData(out=out, files=written, unmatched=unmatched_written)

docs.title: The three models
docs.text:
simple uses counts alone. single adds one sample-sample network. full takes several matched tissues.

Asking for one and getting another is not possible: a request that cannot be honoured raises rather than quietly becoming a different model.

docs.title: preffect.layers
docs.text:
The network pieces the simple model is built from.

Four of them: an encoder and decoder for the counts, and a smaller pair for the library size. The graph versions, which replace the count encoder for the single and full models, arrive with those models.

Each class builds only what it uses. Version 0.1 had one encoder class that constructed the graph path and the plain path together and then chose between them at call time. For a simple model on twenty thousand genes that allocated a graph attention layer of sixteen million parameters which was never touched: measured at 94% of the encoder's weights, 64 MB, initialised on every construction and written into every saved session. Separate classes cost a little duplication and remove all of that.

docs.title: Terms used here
docs.text:
• Encoder maps counts to a small set of numbers, the latent space, that summarise a sample. Decoder maps those numbers back out.
  • Latent space has a mean and a variance per dimension, because the model is variational: it learns a distribution over the summary rather than a single value.
  • Correction variables are things like sequencing batch that the model is told about so it can account for them.
  • FiLM, feature-wise linear modulation, lets a correction variable scale and shift every feature rather than merely being pasted on as extra columns.

docs.title: FiLM
docs.text:
Bases: Module

Scale and shift every feature, by an amount the conditioning decides.

Produces one multiplier and one offset per feature from the conditioning values, so a correction variable can modulate the whole representation instead of being concatenated to it.

Source code in src/preffect/layers.py 
class FiLM(nn.Module):
    """Scale and shift every feature, by an amount the conditioning decides.

    Produces one multiplier and one offset per feature from the conditioning
    values, so a correction variable can modulate the whole representation
    instead of being concatenated to it.
    """

    def __init__(self, n_conditions: int, n_features: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.to_scale_and_shift = nn.Linear(n_conditions, 2 * n_features)

    def forward(self, features: torch.Tensor, conditions: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        scale, shift = self.to_scale_and_shift(conditions.float()).chunk(2, dim=-1)
        return scale * features + shift

docs.text:
Bases: Module

Counts to a latent mean and log variance, for the simple model.

Correction variables are appended to the input and also drive two FiLM layers. Appending them and modulating with them is version 0.1's arrangement and is kept.

Source code in src/preffect/layers.py 
class CountEncoder(nn.Module):
    """Counts to a latent mean and log variance, for the simple model.

    Correction variables are appended to the input and also drive two FiLM
    layers. Appending them and modulating with them is version 0.1's
    arrangement and is kept.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        n_genes: int,
        n_corrections: int,
        hidden_dim: int,
        latent_dim: int,
        leaky_relu_slope: float = 0.2,
        dropout: float = 0.1,
    ):
        super().__init__()
        self.n_corrections = n_corrections
        input_dim = n_genes + n_corrections
        wide = hidden_dim + n_corrections

        self.layer1 = nn.Linear(input_dim, wide)
        self.layer2 = nn.Linear(wide, hidden_dim)
        self.to_mean = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, latent_dim)
        self.to_log_variance = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, latent_dim)

        self.film1 = FiLM(n_corrections, wide) if n_corrections else None
        self.film2 = FiLM(n_corrections, hidden_dim) if n_corrections else None

        self.activation = nn.LeakyReLU(negative_slope=leaky_relu_slope)
        self.dropout1 = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        self.dropout2 = nn.Dropout(dropout)

        self.apply(_orthogonal_init)

    def scale_input(self, counts: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """The scale the first layer sees. See :func:`scale_counts`; a seam for ``exp/10``."""
        return scale_counts(counts)

    def combine_with_corrections(
        self, counts: torch.Tensor, corrections: torch.Tensor | None
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Put the correction variables together with the counts.

        A seam, not a setting. Version 0.1 concatenates their raw values here
        while embedding the categorical ones in the library encoder, with no
        explanation for the difference. Experiment ``exp/02`` overrides this to
        try the embedding treatment in both. See
        ``decisions/2026-10-15_odd_choices_kept_pending_measurement.md``.
        """
        if not self.n_corrections:
            return counts
        if corrections is None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"this encoder was built for {self.n_corrections} correction "
                f"variable(s) but none were supplied"
            )
        return torch.cat((counts, corrections.float()), dim=1)

    def project_to_latent(
        self, hidden: torch.Tensor
    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """Hidden representation to a latent mean and log variance.

        No activation, unlike version 0.1, which applied a leaky rectifier to
        both. ``exp/01`` measured that across eight seeds and found no
        detectable difference in the loss, the reconstruction or the KL
        divergence term, so the simpler and more conventional form was kept.
        See ``decisions/2026-10-15_exp01_latent_rectifier_removed.md``, which
        also records the limit of that evidence: it was measured at 150 genes
        and wants repeating at realistic scale.

        Still a seam, so that repeat costs an hour rather than a day.
        """
        return self.to_mean(hidden), self.to_log_variance(hidden)

    def forward(
        self, counts: torch.Tensor, corrections: torch.Tensor | None = None
    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """:returns: the latent mean and log variance, each ``[samples, latent_dim]``."""
        h = self.combine_with_corrections(self.scale_input(counts), corrections)

        h = self.layer1(h)
        h = torch.nn.functional.elu(h)
        if self.film1 is not None:
            h = self.film1(h, corrections)
        h = self.dropout1(h)

        h = self.layer2(h)
        h = torch.nn.functional.elu(h)
        if self.film2 is not None:
            h = self.film2(h, corrections)
        h = self.dropout2(h)

        return self.project_to_latent(h)

Bases: Module

Latent values back to a hidden representation, for the simple model.

Stops at the hidden layer. The model turns that into distribution parameters, because the three parameters share this representation.

Source code in src/preffect/layers.py 
class CountDecoder(nn.Module):
    """Latent values back to a hidden representation, for the simple model.

    Stops at the hidden layer. The model turns that into distribution
    parameters, because the three parameters share this representation.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        latent_dim: int,
        n_corrections: int,
        hidden_dim: int,
        leaky_relu_slope: float = 0.2,
        dropout: float = 0.1,
    ):
        super().__init__()
        self.n_corrections = n_corrections
        self.layer = nn.Linear(latent_dim + n_corrections, hidden_dim)
        self.film = FiLM(n_corrections, hidden_dim) if n_corrections else None
        self.activation = nn.LeakyReLU(negative_slope=leaky_relu_slope)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        self.apply(_orthogonal_init)

    def forward(
        self, latent: torch.Tensor, corrections: torch.Tensor | None = None
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """:returns: ``[samples, hidden_dim]``."""
        if self.n_corrections:
            if corrections is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"this decoder was built for {self.n_corrections} correction "
                    f"variable(s) but none were supplied"
                )
            h = torch.cat((latent, corrections.float()), dim=1)
        else:
            h = latent

        h = self.activation(self.layer(h))
        if self.film is not None:
            h = self.film(h, corrections)
        return self.dropout(h)

A sample's total count to its own small latent space.

Library size is the total number of reads for a sample, and it varies for reasons that have nothing to do with biology. Modelling it separately lets the rest of the model work on composition instead of absolute depth.

The input is the log of the total, because library sizes span orders of magnitude.

class LibrarySizeEncoder(nn.Module):
    """A sample's total count to its own small latent space.

    Library size is the total number of reads for a sample, and it varies for
    reasons that have nothing to do with biology. Modelling it separately lets
    the rest of the model work on composition instead of absolute depth.

    The input is the log of the total, because library sizes span orders of
    magnitude.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        n_corrections: int,
        hidden_dim: int,
        latent_dim: int,
        leaky_relu_slope: float = 0.2,
        dropout: float = 0.1,
    ):
        super().__init__()
        self.n_corrections = n_corrections
        self.layer = nn.Linear(1 + n_corrections, hidden_dim)
        self.to_mean = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, latent_dim)
        self.to_log_variance = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, latent_dim)
        self.film = FiLM(n_corrections, hidden_dim) if n_corrections else None
        self.activation = nn.LeakyReLU(negative_slope=leaky_relu_slope)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        self.apply(_orthogonal_init)

    def forward(
        self, log_library_size: torch.Tensor, corrections: torch.Tensor | None = None
    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        h = log_library_size.reshape(-1, 1)
        if self.n_corrections:
            if corrections is None:
                raise ValueError("correction variables were expected but not supplied")
            h = torch.cat((h, corrections.float()), dim=1)

        h = self.activation(self.layer(h))
        if self.film is not None:
            h = self.film(h, corrections)
        h = self.dropout(h)
        return self.to_mean(h), self.to_log_variance(h)

docs.text:
scale_counts(counts: Tensor) -> torch.Tensor

What the expression encoder is fed: log(1 + counts).

Version 0.1 fed raw counts, which reach 2.4 million in the DCIS cohort. A learning-rate-sized change to one first-layer weight times an input that size moved the encoder's output a thousandfold in a single step, which was the loss excursion of issue #22 (finding 49). On the log scale the same step moves it by a few thousandths, and the spikes are gone in six seeds of six (exp/10, decision 2026-10-28), with imputation error halved and clustering recovery doubled. The targets, the decoder and the objective still see raw counts; only the encoder's first layer sees this.

A function, not a setting, so there is one behaviour. exp/10's raw arm overrides the encoders' scale_input to feed counts unchanged.

def scale_counts(counts: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """What the expression encoder is fed: ``log(1 + counts)``.

    Version 0.1 fed raw counts, which reach 2.4 million in the DCIS cohort. A
    learning-rate-sized change to one first-layer weight times an input that
    size moved the encoder's output a thousandfold in a single step, which was
    the loss excursion of issue #22 (finding 49). On the log scale the same
    step moves it by a few thousandths, and the spikes are gone in six seeds
    of six (``exp/10``, decision 2026-10-28), with imputation error halved and
    clustering recovery doubled. The targets, the decoder and the objective
    still see raw counts; only the encoder's first layer sees this.

    A function, not a setting, so there is one behaviour. ``exp/10``'s raw arm
    overrides the encoders' ``scale_input`` to feed counts unchanged.
    """
    return torch.log1p(counts)

docs.title: preffect.model
docs.text:
The simple model: counts in, a fitted count distribution out.

The simple model uses the counts alone, with optional correction variables such as sequencing batch. The single and full models add a sample-sample network and matched tissues, and arrive later.

docs.title: What it does, in order
docs.text:
1. The encoder turns a sample's counts into a mean and a variance over a small latent space, a handful of numbers summarising that sample.
  2. Reparameterising draws a point from that distribution in a way that gradients can pass through, so the model can be trained.
  3. The decoder turns the drawn point back into a hidden representation.
  4. Three heads turn that representation into the parameters of a count distribution per gene: the composition, the dispersion, and, for the zero-inflated form, the extra-zero log-odds.
  5. Separately, a library size is either taken from the data or predicted by its own small encoder and decoder. Multiplying the composition by it gives the expected count.

The composition comes out of a softmax, so a sample's predicted proportions sum to one across genes and the library size sets the scale. That split is what lets the model describe what a sample is made of separately from how deeply it was sequenced.

Because the library sets the scale and the composition cannot change it, a library read off a matrix with entries hidden makes every predicted count short by the hidden fraction, and no amount of training can make it up. forward therefore takes a library_scale: the factor that estimates a sample's real total back from how many of its entries were hidden. It is None when nothing is hidden, and the model is then exactly what it was. Finding 56.

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ModelOutput:
    """Everything one forward pass produced.

    Kept whole rather than reduced, because the loss needs the latent
    distribution, inference needs the fitted counts, and diagnostics need both.
    """

    #: Latent summary of each sample: mean, log variance, and the drawn point.
    latent_mean: torch.Tensor
    latent_log_variance: torch.Tensor
    latent: torch.Tensor

    #: Predicted proportion of each sample's counts belonging to each gene.
    #: Sums to one across genes.
    composition: torch.Tensor
    #: Inverse dispersion per gene per sample, positive.
    dispersion: torch.Tensor
    #: Total counts per sample used to scale the composition.
    library_size: torch.Tensor
    #: The fitted distribution over counts.
    counts: NegativeBinomial | ZeroInflatedNegativeBinomial

    #: Log-odds of an extra zero. Present only for the zero-inflated likelihood.
    zero_logits: torch.Tensor | None = None

    #: The library size latent space, present only when it is being inferred.
    library_latent_mean: torch.Tensor | None = None
    library_latent_log_variance: torch.Tensor | None = None
    library_latent: torch.Tensor | None = None
    predicted_log_library_size: torch.Tensor | None = None

    @property
    def infers_library_size(self) -> bool:
        return self.library_latent_mean is not None

    @property
    def expected_counts(self) -> torch.Tensor:
        """The mean of the fitted distribution.

        Returns the product the distribution already holds rather than
        recomputing it. ``_fitted_counts`` multiplies composition by library
        size to build the distribution, and this property used to do the same
        multiplication again on every access, over a samples-by-genes tensor.
        Reading it three times meant three identical multiplications of four
        megabytes.

        It also means the two can no longer disagree. They were computed
        separately from the same inputs, so nothing forced them to match.
        """
        return self.counts.mu
