docs.text: Fitting a model, and recording honestly what happened while it fitted.

docs.title: The number this module exists to get right
docs.text:
An epoch's loss is the mean over its batches. Version 0.1 computed the training loss that way and the validation loss a different way: it divided the accumulated validation loss by the number of tissues, which is one for the simple and single models, so the figure it printed, plotted, sent to TensorBoard and compared against for early stopping was a sum presented as a mean.

That makes it incomparable across batch sizes, because the number of batches changes with the batch size. On four of version 0.1's own run directories, differing only in epochs and batch size, the reported values spanned 33% and the corrected values 4.4%, and the two orderings disagreed.

Here both splits go through the same function, which divides by the number of batches it actually ran, and that count is recorded alongside the loss so the arithmetic can be checked after the fact rather than trusted.

docs.title: Early stopping
docs.text: Off unless asked for. It watches the validation loss and stops when it has not improved by more than a stated amount for a stated number of epochs in a row, restoring the weights from the best epoch. With no validation data it watches the training loss instead and says so, because stopping early on the training loss is a different and weaker thing.

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class SplitResult:
    """What one pass over one split produced."""

    mean_loss: float
    mean_terms: dict[str, float]
    n_batches: int
    n_samples: int

    #: Latent dimensions whose mean actually varies between samples. A latent
    #: space that has collapsed carries no information about which sample is
    #: which, and this is how you see it happen rather than infer it afterwards
    #: from a clustering that found nothing. Finding 41.
    active_latent_units: int = 0
    #: How far the latent means sit from the origin, root mean square. Falling
    #: towards zero alongside active_latent_units is the signature of collapse.
    latent_rms: float = 0.0
    #: How many latent dimensions there are, so the count above has a scale.
    latent_dim: int = 0

    #: The largest total gradient norm over the epoch's steps, measured before
    #: clipping, and the mean. Zero on a measuring pass. Issue #22's excursion
    #: had only ever been seen as a loss sampled every 800 epochs; these say
    #: whether the gradients blew up, which points at a different cause than a
    #: loss that jumped on ordinary gradients.
    largest_gradient_norm: float = 0.0
    mean_gradient_norm: float = 0.0
    #: The largest absolute change to any parameter in the epoch's last step:
    #: what the optimiser did, as opposed to what the gradient asked for. Adam
    #: can turn a small gradient into a large step once its second-moment
    #: estimate has decayed over a long flat stretch. One snapshot per epoch,
    #: so it costs one copy of the parameters rather than one per step.
    largest_update: float = 0.0
    #: Mean relative error on the entries hidden from the model, measured on
    #: the training split after the epoch when early stopping watches it
    #: (``TrainConfig.stop_on``), None otherwise. The number ``exp/10`` and
    #: ``exp/11`` score.
    imputation_error: float | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.n_batches < 1:
            raise ConfigError("a split with no batches has no mean to report")

    @property
    def latent_collapsed(self) -> bool:
        """True when no latent dimension varies between samples."""
        return self.latent_dim > 0 and self.active_latent_units == 0

docs.text:
configure_runtime(config: PreffectConfig) -> None

Apply the runtime settings to PyTorch, once, before building the model.

Before building, not only before train. The seed and the thread count both act at construction: the weights are drawn then, and the sums that draw them run at whatever thread count is in force, so a model built at one count and trained at another is not the model a later call in the same process would build (finding 26 for the seed, issue #23 for the threads). train calls this too, and warns if it finds the thread count changing under a model that already exists.

Set a thread count. PyTorch defaults to one thread per core, which on a large shared machine means a hundred or more. For the tensor sizes PREFFECT works with, coordinating that many threads costs far more than the arithmetic they do. Measured on this project's own graph model, 24 training steps took:

=========== ======== threads time =========== ======== 1 0.082 s 4 0.082 s 16 0.107 s 112 0.200 s =========== ========

Median of five runs on a loaded shared machine, so about two and a half times slower at the default. An earlier version of this docstring said nine hundred times, from a single timing that does not reproduce; see finding 24 for what went wrong with it. Version 0.1 never set the number either, though its vignette notebook does so by hand, which suggests the problem was known and worked around rather than fixed.

The right number depends on the data. A few threads is right for small cohorts; more helps once the matrices are large. Leaving num_threads unset leaves PyTorch alone, which on a shared machine is rarely what you want.

def configure_runtime(config: PreffectConfig) -> None:
    """Apply the runtime settings to PyTorch, once, before building the model.

    Before building, not only before ``train``. The seed and the thread count
    both act at construction: the weights are drawn then, and the sums that
    draw them run at whatever thread count is in force, so a model built at
    one count and trained at another is not the model a later call in the
    same process would build (finding 26 for the seed, issue #23 for the
    threads). ``train`` calls this too, and warns if it finds the thread count
    changing under a model that already exists.

    **Set a thread count.** PyTorch defaults to one thread per core, which on a
    large shared machine means a hundred or more. For the tensor sizes PREFFECT
    works with, coordinating that many threads costs far more than the
    arithmetic they do. Measured on this project's own graph model, 24 training
    steps took:

    ===========  ========
    threads      time
    ===========  ========
    1            0.082 s
    4            0.082 s
    16           0.107 s
    112          0.200 s
    ===========  ========

    Median of five runs on a loaded shared machine, so about two and a half
    times slower at the default. An earlier version of this docstring said nine
    hundred times, from a single timing that does not reproduce; see finding 24
    for what went wrong with it. Version 0.1 never set the number either, though
    its vignette notebook does so by hand, which suggests the problem was known
    and worked around rather than fixed.

    The right number depends on the data. A few threads is right for small
    cohorts; more helps once the matrices are large. Leaving ``num_threads``
    unset leaves PyTorch alone, which on a shared machine is rarely what you
    want.
    """
    if config.runtime.num_threads is not None:
        torch.set_num_threads(config.runtime.num_threads)

    if config.runtime.seed is not None:
        torch.manual_seed(config.runtime.seed)

    if config.runtime.deterministic:
        # Bit-for-bit repeatability, measured on an A100; see the decision
        # record 2026-10-27_gpu_runs_are_deterministic_when_asked.md. The CPU
        # needs the seed alone. A GPU needs four more things: cuBLAS given one
        # fixed workspace, which PyTorch reads from the environment; cuDNN told
        # not to choose its algorithm by timing it; cuDNN's deterministic
        # kernels; and deterministic algorithms everywhere else, which is what
        # makes the graph attention's scatter-add exact. On the single model,
        # 38 of 38 parameter tensors differed between two seeded runs without
        # these and 0 of 38 with them. Setting the workspace variable after
        # CUDA had already been used in the process also worked, measured,
        # though PyTorch's documentation asks for it before launch. setdefault,
        # so that a value chosen in the environment wins.
        os.environ.setdefault("CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG", ":4096:8")
        torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False
        torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True
        # warn_only: an operation with no deterministic kernel warns, naming
        # itself, rather than stopping the run. That is the report issue #9
        # asked for. No operation PREFFECT uses warned.
        torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=True)

    # Refuse a device the machine lacks now, before any data is read. The
    # command line calls this first for exactly that reason.
    resolve_device(config.runtime)

The device a run will use, refused by name if the machine lacks it.

Called by train and by apply before any data is read. A run that asks for a GPU on a machine without one, or for cuda:3 on a machine with two cards, would otherwise fail inside PyTorch after the loading, or, before finding 45, not fail at all: the string was checked and nothing was ever moved, so --device cuda trained on the CPU without a word.

Source code in src/preffect/training.py 
def resolve_device(runtime: RuntimeConfig) -> torch.device:
    """The device a run will use, refused by name if the machine lacks it.

    Called by ``train`` and by ``apply`` before any data is read. A run that
    asks for a GPU on a machine without one, or for ``cuda:3`` on a machine
    with two cards, would otherwise fail inside PyTorch after the loading, or,
    before finding 45, not fail at all: the string was checked and nothing was
    ever moved, so ``--device cuda`` trained on the CPU without a word.
    """
    if not runtime.uses_cuda:
        return torch.device("cpu")
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        raise ConfigError(
            f"device is {runtime.device!r} but this machine has no usable CUDA "
            f"device. Use device='cpu', or run where there is a GPU."
        )
    device = torch.device(runtime.device)
    count = torch.cuda.device_count()
    index = device.index if device.index is not None else 0
    if index >= count:
        raise ConfigError(
            f"device is {runtime.device!r} but this machine has {count} CUDA "
            f"device(s), numbered 0 to {count - 1}."
        )
    return device

def run_epoch(
    model: nn.Module,
    data: TensorData | MultiTissueData,
    config: PreffectConfig,
    epoch: int,
    optimiser: torch.optim.Optimizer | None = None,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
) -> SplitResult:
    """One pass over one split.

    Training and validation share this function deliberately. Version 0.1 wrote
    the two passes out separately, and they drifted: the validation one divided
    by the wrong thing.

    :param data: one split for the simple and single models, or several
        matched tissues for the full model. The two are told apart by type
        rather than by asking a batch what it carries: asking is what stopped
        every full-model run at its first batch (finding 55).
    :param optimiser: supply it to learn, omit it to only measure.
    """
    learning = optimiser is not None
    model.train(learning)

    batches = batch_indices(
        data.n_samples,
        config.train.batch_size,
        rng=rng,
        shuffle=learning and rng is not None,
        drop_last=config.train.drop_last_batch if learning else False,
    )
    if not batches:
        raise ConfigError(
            f"a split of {data.n_samples} samples produced no batches at a batch "
            f"size of {config.train.batch_size}"
        )

    running_total = 0.0
    running_terms: dict[str, float] = {}
    gradient_norms: list[float] = []
    largest_update = 0.0

    seen_latents: list[torch.Tensor] = []
    with torch.set_grad_enabled(learning):
        for index, positions in enumerate(batches):
            part = data.select(positions)
            # The library-size correction for this batch's rows, None when
            # nothing is hidden. Without it a masked batch is scaled by a total
            # short by the hidden fraction while its targets are not, which is
            # finding 56.
            if isinstance(part, MultiTissueData):
                # Several matched tissues: the model takes the list of counts,
                # the target tissue's corrections and one network per tissue,
                # and predicts the target tissue alone. The same shape ``infer``
                # uses on the same data. Until 2026-11-02 this branch did not
                # exist and the loop asked every batch ``has_network``, which a
                # multi-tissue batch does not answer, so the full model stopped
                # at its first batch and had never been trained. Finding 55.
                output = model(
                    [t.inputs for t in part.tissues],
                    part.target.corrections,
                    [t.edge_index for t in part.tissues],
                    library_scale=part.target.library_scale,
                )
                # One observed network per tissue. compute_loss takes a list
                # and gives each tissue its own named term and weight.
                network = [t.adjacency_matrix() for t in part.tissues]
                targets = part.target.targets
                # Which of this batch's rows are real samples, when some
                # patients were missing the predicted tissue and had a row
                # padded in. None when none were, so a complete cohort is
                # scored exactly as it was before padding existed.
                real_rows = part.target_real_rows()
            elif part.has_network:
                output = model(
                    part.inputs,
                    part.corrections,
                    part.edge_index,
                    library_scale=part.library_scale,
                )
                network = part.adjacency_matrix()
                targets = part.targets
                real_rows = None
            else:
                output = model(
                    part.inputs, part.corrections, library_scale=part.library_scale
                )
                network = None
                targets = part.targets
                real_rows = None

            loss = compute_loss(
                output,
                targets,
                weights=config.loss,
                delays=config.delays,
                epoch=epoch,
                batch_labels=None,
                network=network,
                real_rows=real_rows,
            )

            if learning:
                optimiser.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
                loss.total.backward()
                gradient_norms.append(_gradient_norm(model, config.train.gradient_clip_norm))
                last_step = index == len(batches) - 1
                if last_step:
                    tracked = [p for p in model.parameters() if p.grad is not None]
                    before = [p.detach().clone() for p in tracked]
                optimiser.step()
                if last_step:
                    pairs = zip(tracked, before, strict=True)
                    largest_update = max(
                        (float((p.detach() - b).abs().max()) for p, b in pairs), default=0.0
                    )

            seen_latents.append(_latent_means(output))
            running_total += float(loss.total.detach())
            for name, value in loss.named_values().items():
                running_terms[name] = running_terms.get(name, 0.0) + value

    n = len(batches)
    active, rms, latent_dim = _latent_health(seen_latents)
    return SplitResult(
        active_latent_units=active,
        latent_rms=rms,
        latent_dim=latent_dim,
        largest_gradient_norm=max(gradient_norms, default=0.0),
        mean_gradient_norm=sum(gradient_norms) / len(gradient_norms) if gradient_norms else 0.0,
        largest_update=largest_update,
        mean_loss=running_total / n,
        mean_terms={name: total / n for name, total in running_terms.items()},
        n_batches=n,
        n_samples=sum(len(b) for b in batches),
    )

def hidden_entry_scores(model: nn.Module, data: TensorData) -> dict:
    """Everything ``imputation_error`` reports on the entries hidden from the model.

    ``hidden`` is the mean relative error; ``n_hidden`` how many entries it was
    computed over, and ``zero_truth_entries_skipped`` how many of those were
    left out because their true value is zero. Reported together, because an
    error with no count beside it does not say what it was computed over
    (decision of 2026-10-29 on masking).
    """
    from preffect.inference import imputation_error, infer

    if getattr(data, "mask", None) is None:
        raise ConfigError(
            "nothing is hidden in this data, so there is no imputation error to measure"
        )
    device = next(model.parameters()).device
    devices = [device.index] if device.type == "cuda" else []
    with torch.random.fork_rng(devices=devices):
        result = infer(model, data)
    expected = result.expected_counts.detach().cpu()
    hidden = torch.from_numpy(data.mask.hidden)
    return imputation_error(
        expected, data.targets.detach().cpu(), hidden=hidden, kind="mean_relative"
    )

def hidden_entry_error(model: nn.Module, data: TensorData) -> float:
    """Mean relative error on the entries hidden from the model, over a whole split.

    The number ``exp/10`` and ``exp/11`` score: inference in evaluation mode

    forward pass draws random numbers even when the draw is not used, so the

    epoch is the same run as one that does not, stopped sooner or later.
    """
    return hidden_entry_scores(model, data)["hidden"]

def train(
    model: nn.Module,
    train_data: TensorData | MultiTissueData,
    config: PreffectConfig,
    validation_data: TensorData | MultiTissueData | None = None,
    on_epoch=None,
) -> TrainingHistory:
    """Fit a model.

    :param train_data: one split for the simple and single models, or several
        matched tissues for the full model.
    :param on_epoch: called with each :class:`EpochRecord` as it is completed,
        for progress reporting. Reporting is the caller's business; this
        function does not print.
    """
    # The weights were drawn when the model was built, at whatever thread count
    # was in force then. Setting the count now changes nothing about them, but
    # a model built under one count and trained under another is not the model
    # a second call in the same process would build: initialisation sums floats
    # in a different order at a different count, and on this objective that
    # last-bit difference can grow into a different model (issues #22, #23).
    # Nothing can be re-drawn here, so say so, once, naming both counts.
    wanted = config.runtime.num_threads
    if wanted is not None and wanted != torch.get_num_threads():
        warnings.warn(
            f"the model was built while PyTorch was using {torch.get_num_threads()} "
            f"thread(s) and this run will use {wanted}. Starting weights drawn at "
            f"different thread counts differ in their last bits, and on this "
            f"objective that can grow into a different model, so this run may not "
            f"match one where configure_runtime(config) was called before the model "
            f"was built. Call it first. Issue #23.",
            RuntimeWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )

    configure_runtime(config)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(config.runtime.seed)

    # Everything moves to the requested device here, in one place, so that a
    # run which asked for a GPU runs on one. Until finding 45 nothing did, and
    # ``device="cuda"`` trained on the CPU without saying so.
    device = resolve_device(config.runtime)
    model.to(device)
    train_data = train_data.to(device)
    if validation_data is not None:
        validation_data = validation_data.to(device)

    # Only the parameters that are actually being trained. Normally that is all
    # of them; after ``preffect.pretraining.load_pretrained`` froze part of the
    # model it is not. Handing frozen parameters to Adam is harmless but wastes
    # memory on their moment estimates and makes the optimiser's record of what
    # it is training disagree with the model's.
    trainable = [p for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad]
    if not trainable:
        raise ConfigError(
            "every parameter in this model is frozen, so there is nothing to "
            "train. Freeze fewer parts, or load the weights without freezing."
        )
    optimiser = torch.optim.Adam(
        trainable,
        lr=config.train.learning_rate,
        weight_decay=config.train.weight_decay,
    )

    history = TrainingHistory(watched=config.train.stop_on)
    watching_loss = config.train.stop_on == "loss" and config.train.uses_early_stopping
    if watching_loss and validation_data is None:
        history.watched_training_loss = True
    if config.train.stop_on == "imputation" and isinstance(train_data, MultiTissueData):
        # Named rather than left to fall through the message below, which
        # would tell someone to hide entries in data where hiding them is not
        # built. ``workflow.hide_entries`` refuses the same thing in the same
        # terms.
        raise ConfigError(
            "stop_on='imputation' watches the error on entries hidden from the "
            "model, and this is the full model's data: one table per tissue, with "
            "hiding entries across them not built. Stop on the loss, or fit one "
            "tissue with the single model and hide entries there."
        )
    if config.train.stop_on == "imputation" and getattr(train_data, "mask", None) is None:
        raise ConfigError(
            "stop_on='imputation' watches the imputation error on the entries hidden "
            "from the model, and this training data hides none. Hide some "
            "(TensorData(..., mask=mcar_mask(...)) in Python, --hide on the command "
            "line), or stop on the loss."
        )

    best_loss = float("inf")
    best_state: dict | None = None
    epochs_without_improvement = 0

    for epoch in range(1, config.train.epochs + 1):
        train_result = run_epoch(model, train_data, config, epoch, optimiser, rng)
        validation_result = (
            None
            if validation_data is None
            else run_epoch(model, validation_data, config, epoch)
        )
        if config.train.stop_on == "imputation":
            train_result = replace(
                train_result, imputation_error=hidden_entry_error(model, train_data)
            )

        record = EpochRecord(epoch=epoch, train=train_result, validation=validation_result)
        history.epochs.append(record)

        # Say it while it is happening. A collapsed latent carries nothing
        # about which sample is which, so everything downstream of it is
        # describing noise, and the loss does not show it: the expression
        # terms carry on falling. Found by measuring after the fact, which is
        # the hard way. Finding 41.
        if record.train.latent_collapsed and not history.latent_collapsed:
            history.latent_collapsed = True
            history.first_collapsed_epoch = record.epoch
            warnings.warn(
                f"the latent space collapsed at epoch {record.epoch}: none of "
                f"its {record.train.latent_dim} dimensions vary between "
                f"samples any more, so it carries no information about which "
                f"sample is which. The loss will keep falling regardless. "
                f"Consider a KL warm-up through LossDelays, or a lower "
                f"learning rate. See issue #20.",
                stacklevel=2,
            )
        if on_epoch is not None:
            on_epoch(record)

        watched = record.watched_value(config.train.stop_on)
        if watched < best_loss - config.train.early_stopping_min_delta:
            best_loss = watched
            history.best_epoch = epoch
            epochs_without_improvement = 0
            if config.train.uses_early_stopping:
                best_state = copy.deepcopy(model.state_dict())
        else:
            epochs_without_improvement += 1

        if (
            config.train.uses_early_stopping
            and epochs_without_improvement >= config.train.early_stopping_patience
        ):
            history.stopped_early = True
            if best_state is not None:
                model.load_state_dict(best_state)
            break

    return history

docs.text:
Saving and reloading a fitted model.

A checkpoint holds tensors and settings, never a pickled Python object.

Version 0.1 saved a session with torch.save(self), pickling the whole live object: the model, the optimiser, the datasets and the settings together. PyTorch 2.6 changed torch.load to refuse pickled objects by default, so every session version 0.1 ever wrote becomes unreadable the moment anyone upgrades. The warning announcing that change was suppressed in version 0.1 rather than acted on.

Pickling the live object had two further costs. The file carried the training data, so a checkpoint of a small model on a large cohort was enormous and quietly contained the cohort. And it carried whatever layers the model had allocated and never used, which for a simple model was 94% of the encoder.

Here a checkpoint is a plain dictionary of tensors and plain values. It loads under PyTorch's safe default, it does not contain anybody's data, and it can be read by a version of the code that is not the one that wrote it, because the settings travel with it and are checked on the way back in.

docs.text:
How the run that produced a model went, as plain numbers and sentences.

A saved model says what it is but not how it came to be, and the two questions a reader asks of a fit are whether it had finished moving and whether it was stopped early. This carries the answer: the loss at every epoch for each split, when it stopped and why, and how long it took.

It is not the whole training history. The per-epoch diagnostics that :class:~preffect.training.TrainingHistory collects, such as the gradient norms and whether the latent space collapsed, are left out. Keeping a few of its fields and defaulting the rest would hand a reader numbers that nothing measured.

Source code in src/preffect/checkpoint.py 
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class TrainingRecord:
    """How the run that produced a model went, as plain numbers and sentences.

    A saved model says what it is but not how it came to be, and the two
    questions a reader asks of a fit are whether it had finished moving and
    whether it was stopped early. This carries the answer: the loss at every
    epoch for each split, when it stopped and why, and how long it took.

    **It is not the whole training history.** The per-epoch diagnostics that
    :class:`~preffect.training.TrainingHistory` collects, such as the gradient
    norms and whether the latent space collapsed, are left out. Keeping a few
    of its fields and defaulting the rest would hand a reader numbers that
    nothing measured.
    """

    #: Epoch numbers, starting at one, one per entry of the losses below.
    epochs: tuple[int, ...]
    #: Mean loss per batch over the training split, one per epoch.
    train_loss: tuple[float, ...]
    #: The same over the validation split, or ``None`` if none was given.
    validation_loss: tuple[float, ...] | None
    #: Epochs actually run, and epochs asked for. They differ after an early stop.
    n_epochs: int
    epochs_asked_for: int
    #: True when early stopping ended the run before its last epoch.
    stopped_early: bool
    #: The epoch whose weights were saved, which after an early stop is the
    #: best one rather than the last.
    best_epoch: int | None
    #: What early stopping watched: ``"loss"`` or ``"imputation"``.
    watched: str
    #: True when early stopping had to watch the training loss for want of a
    #: validation split, which is a weaker thing to stop on.
    watched_training_loss: bool
    #: One sentence saying how the run ended, ready to show to a reader.
    stop_reason: str
    #: Wall-clock seconds spent fitting, excluding reading the data.
    wall_seconds: float

    @classmethod
    def from_extra(cls, extra: dict[str, Any] | None) -> TrainingRecord | None:
        """Read the record out of a checkpoint's ``extra``, or ``None``.

        ``None`` means the model was saved before its history was kept, which
        is an ordinary thing for an older file and not an error.
        """
        stored = (extra or {}).get(TRAINING_HISTORY_KEY)
        if not isinstance(stored, dict) or "train_loss" not in stored:
            return None
        validation = stored.get("validation_loss")
        return cls(
            epochs=tuple(int(e) for e in stored.get("epochs", ())),
            train_loss=tuple(float(v) for v in stored["train_loss"]),
            validation_loss=(
                None if validation is None else tuple(float(v) for v in validation)
            ),
            n_epochs=int(stored.get("n_epochs", len(stored["train_loss"]))),
            epochs_asked_for=int(stored.get("epochs_asked_for", 0)),
            stopped_early=bool(stored.get("stopped_early", False)),
            best_epoch=(
                None if stored.get("best_epoch") is None else int(stored["best_epoch"])
            ),
            watched=str(stored.get("watched", "loss")),
            watched_training_loss=bool(stored.get("watched_training_loss", False)),
            stop_reason=str(stored.get("stop_reason", "")),
            wall_seconds=float(stored.get("wall_seconds", 0.0)),
        )

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Checkpoint:
    """What was read back from a file."""

    model_state: dict[str, torch.Tensor]
    model_config: ModelConfig
    n_genes: int
    gene_names: tuple[str, ...] | None
    optimiser_state: dict[str, Any] | None
    written_by: str
    format_version: int
    extra: dict[str, Any]
    #: Every setting the run used, as plain values, or ``None`` for a file
    #: written without them. Provenance: paths in it are the training
    #: machine's and are never used to find anything on reloading.
    full_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None

    @property
    def training(self) -> TrainingRecord | None:
        """How the run that wrote this file went, or ``None`` if it was not kept."""
        return TrainingRecord.from_extra(self.extra)

    def build_model(self):
        """Reconstruct the model and load its weights.

        The kind travels in the settings and the tissue count beside them, so
        a single or full model comes back as itself. This built a simple model
        whatever the file said until 2026-11-02, which for a graph model meant
        a PyTorch error about unexpected keys rather than a sentence, and
        nothing had reloaded a full model to find out (finding 55).
        """
        from preffect.errors import CheckpointError
        from preffect.workflow import build_model

        n_tissues = int(self.extra.get("n_tissues", 1))
        if self.model_config.kind.value == "full" and n_tissues < 2:
            raise CheckpointError(
                f"this checkpoint says it holds a full model but records "
                f"{n_tissues} tissue(s); the full model combines at least 2. The "
                f"file was written without its tissue count."
            )
        model = build_model(
            self.model_config.kind, self.n_genes, self.model_config, n_tissues
        )
        model.load_state_dict(self.model_state)
        return model

def training_history_record(
    history,
    *,
    epochs_asked_for: int,
    wall_seconds: float,
    patience: int | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Reduce a training history to the plain values a checkpoint carries.

    Every value here is a number, a string or a list of them, so it survives
    PyTorch's safe loader and comes back without unpickling anything. Hand the
    result to :func:`save_checkpoint` under :data:`TRAINING_HISTORY_KEY` and
    read it back with :meth:`TrainingRecord.from_extra`.

    :param history: a :class:`~preffect.training.TrainingHistory`.
    :param epochs_asked_for: the epoch count the run was given, which after an
        early stop is larger than the number run.
    :param wall_seconds: how long the fit took, excluding reading the data.
    :param patience: the early-stopping patience in force, or ``None``.
    """
    validation = [
        float(record.validation.mean_loss)
        for record in history.epochs
        if record.validation is not None
    ]
    return {
        "epochs": [int(record.epoch) for record in history.epochs],
        "train_loss": [float(record.train.mean_loss) for record in history.epochs],
        "validation_loss": validation if validation else None,
        "n_epochs": len(history.epochs),
        "epochs_asked_for": int(epochs_asked_for),
        "stopped_early": bool(history.stopped_early),
        "best_epoch": history.best_epoch,
        "watched": str(history.watched),
        "watched_training_loss": bool(history.watched_training_loss),
        "stop_reason": _stop_reason(history, epochs_asked_for, patience),
        "wall_seconds": float(wall_seconds),
    }

def save_checkpoint(
    path: str | Path,
    model: nn.Module,
    model_config: ModelConfig,
    n_genes: int,
    gene_names: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
    optimiser: torch.optim.Optimizer | None = None,
    full_config: PreffectConfig | None = None,
    **extra: Any,
) -> Path:
    """Write a model to disk.

    :param gene_names: the genes the model was fitted on, in order. Strongly
        worth supplying: without them nothing can check that the data a loaded
        model is applied to has its columns in the same order, which is the
        mistake version 0.1 made within a single run.
    :param full_config: recorded for the provenance of the run. Paths in it are
        stored as text and are not used on loading.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    payload = {
        "format_version": CHECKPOINT_FORMAT,
        "written_by": __version__,
        "model_state": model.state_dict(),
        "model_config": _plain(model_config),
        "n_genes": n_genes,
        "gene_names": list(gene_names) if gene_names is not None else None,
        "optimiser_state": optimiser.state_dict() if optimiser is not None else None,
        "full_config": _plain(full_config) if full_config is not None else None,
        "extra": _plain(extra),
    }
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    torch.save(payload, path)
    return path

def load_checkpoint(path: str | Path) -> Checkpoint:
    """Read a model back.

    Loads with PyTorch's safe default, which refuses arbitrary pickled objects.

    :raises CheckpointError: if the file is missing, was written by an
        incompatible format, or is one of version 0.1's pickled sessions.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    if not path.is_file():
        raise CheckpointError(f"no checkpoint at {path}")

    try:
        payload = torch.load(path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - the cause is reported verbatim
        raise CheckpointError(
            f"could not read {path}: {exc}. If this file was written by PREFFECT "
            f"0.1, it is a pickled Python object rather than a set of tensors, and "
            f"current PyTorch will not load it. Retrain, or load it with PREFFECT "
            f"0.1 under its own environment and export the weights."
        ) from exc

    if not isinstance(payload, dict) or "format_version" not in payload:
        raise CheckpointError(
            f"{path} is not a PREFFECT checkpoint: it has no format version."
        )

    found = payload["format_version"]
    if found != CHECKPOINT_FORMAT:
        raise CheckpointError(
            f"{path} is checkpoint format {found} and this is PREFFECT "
            f"{__version__}, which reads format {CHECKPOINT_FORMAT}."
        )

    config_values = dict(payload["model_config"])
    config_values["correction_variables"] = tuple(
        CorrectionVariable(**v) for v in config_values.get("correction_variables", [])
    )
    # ModelConfig coerces the enum fields back from their stored strings.
    model_config = ModelConfig(**config_values)

    gene_names = payload.get("gene_names")
    full_config = payload.get("full_config")
    return Checkpoint(
        model_state=payload["model_state"],
        model_config=model_config,
        n_genes=int(payload["n_genes"]),
        gene_names=tuple(gene_names) if gene_names is not None else None,
        optimiser_state=payload.get("optimiser_state"),
        written_by=payload.get("written_by", "unknown"),
        format_version=found,
        extra=payload.get("extra", {}),
        full_config=dict(full_config) if isinstance(full_config, dict) else None,
    )

docs.title: preffect.inference
docs.text:
Applying a fitted model: cleaned counts, latent summaries, imputation.

Training fits the model. Inference uses it: run data through and keep what comes out, as cleaned counts to hand to an ordinary analysis, as a latent summary to cluster in, or as filled-in values where counts were missing.

docs.title: Truth is passed in, never looked up
docs.text:
:func:imputation_error takes the true values as an argument. It cannot find them for you, and that is the whole point.

Version 0.1 looked for a layer called truth in the input, and if it was not there the data loader quietly made one up: the per-gene mean across samples. The error routine then compared the model against that, in a column it labelled truth_mu. On any real dataset, which carries no simulation parameters, this reported distance from the gene mean under the name of imputation accuracy, and nothing warned. That is finding 10.

Here there is nowhere for a fabricated truth to come from. If you have no true values you cannot call the function, which is the correct outcome.

docs.title: Rows that stand in for a missing tissue are not reported
docs.text: The full model can be given a cohort where some patients lack the tissue it predicts. A row of per-gene means stands in for each of those patients so the rest of the cohort can be encoded, and :func:infer drops those rows from everything it returns and says how many it dropped. Reporting a cleaned count for a profile nobody measured is the sort of thing finding 10 was about.

docs.title: Inference uses the latent mean, not a draw
docs.text: Version 0.1 ran inference through the same path as training, which samples from the latent distribution, so running the same model over the same data twice gave different cleaned counts. Here the latent mean is used by default, so the output is deterministic and a result can be reproduced. Pass sample_latent=True for version 0.1's behaviour, which is what you want if you are deliberately drawing several times to see the spread.

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class InferenceResult:
    """What a fitted model made of some data."""

    #: Expected counts: the model's cleaned view of the input.
    expected_counts: torch.Tensor
    #: Predicted proportion of each sample's counts per gene, summing to one.
    composition: torch.Tensor
    #: Inverse dispersion per gene per sample.
    dispersion: torch.Tensor
    #: Total counts per sample used to scale the composition.
    library_size: torch.Tensor
    #: Latent summary per sample, the thing worth clustering in.
    latent: torch.Tensor
    #: Log-odds of an extra zero, for the zero-inflated likelihood only.
    zero_logits: torch.Tensor | None = None
    #: True when the latent mean was used rather than a draw from it.
    deterministic: bool = True
    #: How many rows were left out because they were padding rather than
    #: samples. The full model can be given a cohort where some patients lack
    #: the predicted tissue; a row of per-gene means stands in for each while
    #: the model runs, and nothing about it is reported here. Zero for every
    #: other case. See :mod:`preffect.data.tissues`.
    n_padded_rows_dropped: int = 0

    @property
    def n_samples(self) -> int:
        return self.expected_counts.shape[0]

    @property
    def n_genes(self) -> int:
        return self.expected_counts.shape[1]

    def to_anndata(
        self,
        sample_names: list[str] | None = None,
        gene_names: list[str] | None = None,
    ):
        """Package the result as an AnnData, for handing to other tools.

        ``X`` holds the expected counts. The rest travel as layers and as
        ``obsm`` so nothing has to be recomputed.
        """
        import anndata as ad
        import pandas as pd

        def frame(names, n, prefix):
            index = names if names is not None else [f"{prefix}{i}" for i in range(n)]
            if len(index) != n:

                    f"got {len(index)} {prefix}names for {n} {prefix}s"

            # string array, which anndata 0.11 refuses to write without an
            # opt-in, so `preffect apply` crashed at its last line in a fresh
            # install while passing in this repository's newer environment.
            # Finding 48.
            return pd.DataFrame(index=pd.Index(list(index), dtype=object))

        adata = ad.AnnData(
            X=self.expected_counts.detach().cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32),
            obs=frame(sample_names, self.n_samples, "sample_"),
            var=frame(gene_names, self.n_genes, "gene_"),
        )
        adata.layers["composition"] = self.composition.detach().cpu().numpy()
        adata.layers["dispersion"] = self.dispersion.detach().cpu().numpy()
        if self.zero_logits is not None:
            adata.layers["zero_logits"] = self.zero_logits.detach().cpu().numpy()
        adata.obsm["latent"] = self.latent.detach().cpu().numpy()
        adata.obs["library_size"] = self.library_size.detach().cpu().numpy().ravel()
        adata.uns["deterministic"] = self.deterministic
        adata.uns["padded_rows_dropped"] = self.n_padded_rows_dropped

def to_anndata(

    ``X`` holds the expected counts. The rest travel as layers and as
    ``obsm`` so nothing has to be recomputed.

    import anndata as ad

        if len(index) != n:

        # string array, which anndata 0.11 refuses to write without an
        # opt-in, so `preffect apply` crashed at its last line in a fresh
        # install while passing in this repository's newer environment.
        # Finding 48.
        return pd.DataFrame(index=pd.Index(list(index), dtype=object))

    adata = ad.AnnData(
        X=self.expected_counts.detach().cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32),
        obs=frame(sample_names, self.n_samples, "sample_"),
        var=frame(gene_names, self.n_genes, "gene_"),
    )
    adata.layers["composition"] = self.composition.detach().cpu().numpy()

docs.title: NetworkRecovery dataclass
docs.text:
How well a predicted sample-sample network matches the observed one.

Every number is over the pairs of distinct samples, each pair counted once. Two baselines are worth holding beside the scores. A model that predicts no edge anywhere predicts nothing, so its precision, recall and F1 are all zero. A model that cannot rank the pairs at all, whether it predicts no edge, every edge, or one half everywhere, has an average precision equal to the density, which is why the density is carried here under both names.

Source code in src/preffect/inference.py 
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class NetworkRecovery:
    """How well a predicted sample-sample network matches the observed one.

    Every number is over the pairs of distinct samples, each pair counted once.
    Two baselines are worth holding beside the scores. A model that predicts
    no edge anywhere predicts nothing, so its precision, recall and F1 are all
    zero. A model that cannot rank the pairs at all, whether it predicts no
    edge, every edge, or one half everywhere, has an average precision equal to
    the density, which is why the density is carried here under both names.
    """

    #: Of the pairs predicted to be edges, the share that are. Zero when nothing
    #: is predicted.
    precision: float
    #: Of the observed edges, the share predicted.
    recall: float
    #: The harmonic mean of the two; zero when either is.
    f1: float
    #: Precision averaged over the ranking of every pair by its probability,
    #: so it needs no threshold. One when every edge outranks every non-edge.
    average_precision: float
    #: The share of pairs that are edges in the observed network.
    density: float
    #: What a prediction that ranks nothing scores on average precision: the
    #: density. The number ``average_precision`` has to beat.
    flat_average_precision: float
    #: The pairs scored, the observed edges among them, and the pairs predicted
    #: to be edges at the threshold of one half.
    n_pairs: int
    n_edges: int
    n_predicted: int

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return (
            f"precision {self.precision:.3f}, recall {self.recall:.3f}, F1 {self.f1:.3f} "
            f"at one half ({self.n_predicted} pairs predicted, {self.n_edges} edges "
            f"among {self.n_pairs} pairs); average precision {self.average_precision:.3f} "
            f"against {self.flat_average_precision:.3f} for a flat prediction"
        )

one row per real sample of the predicted tissue. Where the full model was given a cohort with patients missing that tissue, a row of per-gene means stood in for each of them so that the rest of the cohort could be encoded; those rows are dropped here and counted in n_padded_rows_dropped, because nothing in them was measured.

@torch.no_grad()
def infer(
    model: nn.Module,
    data,
    sample_latent: bool = False,
) -> InferenceResult:
    """Run a fitted model over some data.

    Runs the whole split in one pass rather than in mini-batches: there is no
    optimiser step, so there is nothing to gain by dividing it, and batching
    would cut the sample-sample network down for no reason. See finding 22.

    :param data: a :class:`~preffect.data.tensors.TensorData` for the simple
        and single models, or a
        :class:`~preffect.data.tissues.MultiTissueData` for the full model.
    :param sample_latent: draw from the latent distribution instead of using
        its mean. Off by default, so the same model over the same data gives
        the same answer twice.
    :returns: one row per **real** sample of the predicted tissue. Where the
        full model was given a cohort with patients missing that tissue, a row
        of per-gene means stood in for each of them so that the rest of the
        cohort could be encoded; those rows are dropped here and counted in
        ``n_padded_rows_dropped``, because nothing in them was measured.
    """
    from preffect.data.tissues import MultiTissueData

    # Where the model is, the data goes. ``train`` moves its own copy of the
    # data to the device and the caller's copy stays where it was, so the
    # natural sequence of fitting on a GPU and then calling this with the same
    # data failed on a device mismatch with a PyTorch error, not a sentence.
    # Finding 45's third half.
    data = data.to(next(model.parameters()).device)

    was_training = model.training
    model.eval()
    try:
        # The library-size correction travels with the data, as the factor that
        # estimates back what hiding entries took off each sample's total. It
        # is None when nothing was hidden. For the full model it is the target
        # tissue's, since that is the only tissue whose counts are predicted.
        # Finding 56.
        real_rows = None
        if isinstance(data, MultiTissueData):
            counts = [t.inputs for t in data.tissues]
            corrections = data.target.corrections
            library_scale = data.target.library_scale
            output = model(
                counts,
                corrections,
                [t.edge_index for t in data.tissues],
                library_scale=library_scale,
            )
            target_counts = counts[0]
            # Every row goes through the model, padding included, because a
            # padded row is a node of the network the real rows attend over.
            # Only the results are cut down, below.
            real_rows = data.target_real_rows()
        else:
            corrections = data.corrections
            target_counts = data.inputs
            library_scale = data.library_scale
            if data.has_network:
                output = model(
                    data.inputs, corrections, data.edge_index, library_scale=library_scale
                )
            else:
                output = model(data.inputs, corrections, library_scale=library_scale)

        if sample_latent:
            latent = output.latent
        else:
            # Decode again from the mean, so every reported quantity comes from
            # the same latent values rather than the composition coming from a
            # draw and the summary from the mean.
            latent = output.latent_mean
            output = model._finish_counts(  # noqa: SLF001 - the model's own helper
                target_counts,
                corrections,
                latent,
                output.latent_mean,
                output.latent_log_variance,
                library_scale=library_scale,
            )
    finally:
        model.train(was_training)

    def keep(value: torch.Tensor | None) -> torch.Tensor | None:
        if value is None or real_rows is None:
            return value
        return value[real_rows]

    return InferenceResult(
        expected_counts=keep(output.expected_counts),
        composition=keep(output.composition),
        dispersion=keep(output.dispersion),
        library_size=keep(output.library_size),
        latent=keep(latent),
        zero_logits=keep(output.zero_logits),
        deterministic=not sample_latent,
        n_padded_rows_dropped=0 if real_rows is None else int((~real_rows).sum()),
    )

How well the fitted distribution explains each sample, one number per sample.

The mean log probability per gene of that sample's observed counts under the distribution the model fitted for it. Per gene rather than summed over genes, so the number does not grow with the size of the panel and two cohorts can be compared.

Larger is better, and every value is negative, because these are probabilities of a particular count. The number on its own means little; what it is for is ranking the cohort. A sample far below the rest is one the model cannot account for, and the three usual reasons are a failed library, a mislabelled sample, and a sample of a different tissue.

The distribution is rebuilt from what :func:infer returned, so it is the same negative binomial, or zero-inflated negative binomial, that the objective was computed with.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default observed

the counts the model was given, samples by genes.

required

Raises:

Type Description PreffectError

if the counts are not the shape the result is.

Source code in src/preffect/inference.py 
def log_likelihood_per_sample(result: InferenceResult, observed) -> np.ndarray:
    """How well the fitted distribution explains each sample, one number per sample.

    The mean log probability **per gene** of that sample's observed counts
    under the distribution the model fitted for it. Per gene rather than
    summed over genes, so the number does not grow with the size of the panel
    and two cohorts can be compared.

    Larger is better, and every value is negative, because these are
    probabilities of a particular count. The number on its own means little;
    what it is for is ranking the cohort. A sample far below the rest is one
    the model cannot account for, and the three usual reasons are a failed
    library, a mislabelled sample, and a sample of a different tissue.

    The distribution is rebuilt from what :func:`infer` returned, so it is the
    same negative binomial, or zero-inflated negative binomial, that the
    objective was computed with.

    :param observed: the counts the model was given, samples by genes.
    :raises PreffectError: if the counts are not the shape the result is.
    """
    from preffect.distributions import (
        NegativeBinomial,
        ZeroInflatedNegativeBinomial,
    )

    counts = _as_tensor(observed)
    mu = result.expected_counts.detach().cpu().float()
    if counts.shape != mu.shape:
        raise PreffectError(
            f"the counts are shaped {tuple(counts.shape)} and the fitted means "
            f"{tuple(mu.shape)}; they have to match"
        )
    theta = result.dispersion.detach().cpu().float()
    if result.zero_logits is None:
        fitted = NegativeBinomial(mu=mu, theta=theta)
    else:
        fitted = ZeroInflatedNegativeBinomial(
            mu=mu, theta=theta, zero_logits=result.zero_logits.detach().cpu().float()
        )
    return fitted.log_prob(counts).mean(dim=1).detach().cpu().numpy()

How closely fitted follows observed across the samples, one number per gene.

Pearson correlation down each column: for one gene, the observed count in every sample against the count the model fitted for that same sample. One means the model tracks that gene's variation across the cohort perfectly, and zero means it predicts the same thing for every sample.

A gene that is constant in the counts, or constant in the fit, has no correlation to report and comes back as nan rather than as a zero that would read as a failure. Take the median over the genes that are not nan for a single number describing a fit.

def correlation_per_gene(result: InferenceResult, observed) -> np.ndarray:
    """How closely fitted follows observed across the samples, one number per gene.

    Pearson correlation down each column: for one gene, the observed count in
    every sample against the count the model fitted for that same sample. One
    means the model tracks that gene's variation across the cohort perfectly,
    and zero means it predicts the same thing for every sample.

    A gene that is constant in the counts, or constant in the fit, has no
    correlation to report and comes back as ``nan`` rather than as a zero that
    would read as a failure. Take the median over the genes that are not
    ``nan`` for a single number describing a fit.

    :param observed: the counts the model was given, samples by genes.
    :raises PreffectError: if the counts are not the shape the result is.
    """
    counts = _as_tensor(observed).numpy()
    fitted = result.expected_counts.detach().cpu().float().numpy()
    if counts.shape != fitted.shape:
        raise PreffectError(
            f"the counts are shaped {counts.shape} and the fitted counts "
            f"{fitted.shape}; they have to match"
        )
    centred_observed = counts - counts.mean(axis=0)
    centred_fitted = fitted - fitted.mean(axis=0)
    # Spread of zero means the correlation is undefined, not zero. Dividing
    # anyway would turn "this gene never moves" into "the model got it wrong".
    spread = np.sqrt((centred_observed**2).sum(axis=0) * (centred_fitted**2).sum(axis=0))
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        correlation = (centred_observed * centred_fitted).sum(axis=0) / spread
    correlation[spread == 0] = np.nan
    return correlation

def imputation_error(
    predicted: torch.Tensor,
    truth: torch.Tensor,
    hidden: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    kind: str = "mean_squared",
) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Compare filled-in values against values that are actually known.

    :param predicted: the model's expected counts.
    :param truth: the real values. **Required, and never inferred.** If you do
        not have them, you cannot measure imputation accuracy, and version
        0.1's habit of substituting the per-gene mean is why this is spelled
        out. See finding 10.
    :param hidden: boolean mask of the entries that were hidden from the model.
        When given, the error is reported separately for hidden and visible
        entries, which is the comparison that means anything: doing well on
        entries the model was shown is not imputation.
    :param kind: ``mean_squared`` or ``mean_relative``.
    :raises PreffectError: on a shape mismatch or an unknown kind.
    """
    if predicted.shape != truth.shape:
        raise PreffectError(
            f"predicted is shaped {tuple(predicted.shape)} and truth "
            f"{tuple(truth.shape)}; they have to match"
        )
    if kind not in ("mean_squared", "mean_relative"):
        raise PreffectError(
            f"kind must be 'mean_squared' or 'mean_relative', got {kind!r}"
        )

    predicted = predicted.detach().float()
    truth = truth.detach().float()

    def score(a: torch.Tensor, b: torch.Tensor) -> float:
        if a.numel() == 0:
            return float("nan")
        if kind == "mean_squared":
            return float(((a - b) ** 2).mean())
        # Relative error is undefined where the true value is zero, and count
        # data is 10 to 55 per cent zeros. Version 0.1 divided by
        # ``truth + 1e-8``, which makes a zero-truth entry contribute up to a
        # hundred million. It rarely fired there, because version 0.1 compared
        # against smoothed per-gene means rather than counts, and a per-gene
        # mean is zero only for a gene that is zero in every sample: one such
        # gene exists across the nine datasets. Comparing against actual
        # counts, which is the correct thing, makes it ordinary. Those entries
        # are left out and counted. See finding 25.
        nonzero = b != 0
        if not nonzero.any():
            return float("nan")
        return float((a[nonzero] - b[nonzero]).abs().div(b[nonzero].abs()).mean())

    if hidden is not None and hidden.shape != truth.shape:
        raise PreffectError(
            f"the mask is shaped {tuple(hidden.shape)} and truth "
            f"{tuple(truth.shape)}; they have to match"
        )
    result = {"overall": score(predicted, truth)}
    if kind == "mean_relative":
        # Counted over the entries that were scored: the hidden ones when a
        # mask is given, the whole matrix otherwise. It used to be counted over
        # the whole matrix whatever was scored (finding 53).
        scored = truth[hidden] if hidden is not None else truth
        skipped = int((scored == 0).sum())
        result["zero_truth_entries_skipped"] = skipped
        result["fraction_skipped"] = skipped / scored.numel() if scored.numel() else 0.0

    if hidden is not None:
        result["hidden"] = score(predicted[hidden], truth[hidden])
        result["visible"] = score(predicted[~hidden], truth[~hidden])
        result["n_hidden"] = int(hidden.sum())

    return result

network_recovery(
    predicted: Tensor, observed: Tensor
) -> NetworkRecovery

Score a predicted sample-sample network against the observed one.

The loss cannot say whether the network is being recovered: on a network one per cent dense, a model that predicts no edge anywhere scores well on an unweighted cross-entropy (issue #13). This scores the edges directly.

Both inputs are square over the same samples, the prediction a matrix of edge probabilities and the observation a 0/1 matrix. Both are read as symmetric: each pair of distinct samples is taken once, from above the diagonal, and the diagonal is ignored, since a sample's link to itself is not a pair and the loader never carries one. An edge is predicted where the probability exceeds one half; at exactly one half the model is undecided and no edge is counted, which is what the inner-product decoder produces when its latent has collapsed.

Average precision is computed here rather than imported: sort the pairs by probability, and average the precision at each distinct probability over the recall it adds, which is the usual definition and treats tied probabilities as one threshold.

Raises:

Type Description PreffectError

if the shapes differ, are not square, or the observed network is not symmetric.

Source code in src/preffect/inference.py 
def network_recovery(predicted: torch.Tensor, observed: torch.Tensor) -> NetworkRecovery:
    """Score a predicted sample-sample network against the observed one.

    The loss cannot say whether the network is being recovered: on a network
    one per cent dense, a model that predicts no edge anywhere scores well on
    an unweighted cross-entropy (issue #13). This scores the edges directly.

    Both inputs are square over the same samples, the prediction a matrix of
    edge probabilities and the observation a 0/1 matrix. Both are read as
    symmetric: each pair of distinct samples is taken once, from above the
    diagonal, and the diagonal is ignored, since a sample's link to itself is
    not a pair and the loader never carries one. An edge is predicted where the
    probability exceeds one half; at exactly one half the model is undecided
    and no edge is counted, which is what the inner-product decoder produces
    when its latent has collapsed.

    Average precision is computed here rather than imported: sort the pairs by
    probability, and average the precision at each distinct probability over
    the recall it adds, which is the usual definition and treats tied
    probabilities as one threshold.

    :raises PreffectError: if the shapes differ, are not square, or the
        observed network is not symmetric.
    """
    predicted = predicted.detach().float().cpu()
    observed = observed.detach().float().cpu()
    if predicted.shape != observed.shape or predicted.dim() != 2:
        raise PreffectError(
            f"predicted is shaped {tuple(predicted.shape)} and observed "
            f"{tuple(observed.shape)}; both must be square over the same samples"
        )
    n = observed.shape[0]
    if observed.shape != (n, n):
        raise PreffectError(f"the network is shaped {tuple(observed.shape)}, not square")
    if not torch.equal(observed > 0, observed.t() > 0):
        raise PreffectError(
            "the observed network is not symmetric; the models score undirected "
            "networks, with both directions of every edge present"
        )

    rows, cols = torch.triu_indices(n, n, offset=1)
    scores = predicted[rows, cols]
    truth = observed[rows, cols] > 0
    n_pairs = int(truth.numel())
    n_edges = int(truth.sum())
    density = n_edges / n_pairs if n_pairs else 0.0

    called = scores > 0.5
    n_predicted = int(called.sum())
    hits = int((called & truth).sum())
    precision = hits / n_predicted if n_predicted else 0.0
    recall = hits / n_edges if n_edges else 0.0
    f1 = 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall) if precision + recall else 0.0

    if n_edges and n_pairs:
        order = torch.argsort(scores, descending=True)
        ranked_scores = scores[order]
        ranked_truth = truth[order].float()
        true_so_far = torch.cumsum(ranked_truth, dim=0)
        seen_so_far = torch.arange(1, n_pairs + 1, dtype=torch.float32)
        # The last position of each run of equal scores is one threshold; the
        # precision and recall there are what a cut at that score would give.
        last_of_run = torch.ones(n_pairs, dtype=torch.bool)
        last_of_run[:-1] = ranked_scores[:-1] != ranked_scores[1:]
        precision_at = (true_so_far / seen_so_far)[last_of_run]
        recall_at = (true_so_far / n_edges)[last_of_run]
        recall_before = torch.cat([recall_at.new_zeros(1), recall_at[:-1]])
        average_precision = float(((recall_at - recall_before) * precision_at).sum())
    else:
        average_precision = 0.0

    return NetworkRecovery(
        precision=precision,
        recall=recall,
        f1=f1,
        average_precision=average_precision,
        density=density,
        flat_average_precision=density,
        n_pairs=n_pairs,
        n_edges=n_edges,
        n_predicted=n_predicted,
    )

class SplitReport:
    """What :func:`inspect_split` found: the tissues, and what would stop a run.

    ``problem`` is the sentence a run would have refused with, or ``None`` if
    the counts look usable. The tissues are listed even when there is a
    problem, whenever they could be read at all, so a reader sees what was
    there.
    """

    folder: Path
    tissues: tuple[TissueSummary, ...]
    problem: str | None = None

    @property
    def usable(self) -> bool:
        """True if nothing would stop a run on this split."""
        return self.problem is None

def read_split(folder: Path, n_tissues: int, unmatched: str = "pad"):
    """Read a split, check it, and align the tissues if there are several.

    :param unmatched: what to do about a patient with no sample in some
        tissue, passed straight to
        :func:`~preffect.data.tissues.align_tissues`. The default pads a row
        in; ``"refuse"`` stops instead, so a caller can drop the incomplete
        patients and work with a complete cohort.
    :returns: the tissues. Which rows were padded in travels with them, in the
        sample annotation :data:`~preffect.data.tissues.GHOST_COLUMN`, which
        is what :func:`to_model_data` reads.
    :raises PreffectError: if the folder is missing, holds no count files, or
        the counts would stop a run.
    """
    from preffect.data.checks import check_tissues
    from preffect.data.loading import load_tissues
    from preffect.data.tissues import align_tissues

    tissues = load_tissues(folder, n_tissues)
    check_tissues(tissues, split=folder.name)
    if n_tissues <= 1:
        return tissues
    return align_tissues(tissues, split=folder.name, unmatched=unmatched).tissues

def to_model_data(tissues, model_config, with_network: bool):
    """Turn checked tissues into what a model takes: one bundle, or one per tissue.

    Several tissues come back as a bundle carrying which of their rows were
    padded in for a patient missing that tissue, read from the annotation
    :func:`~preffect.data.tissues.align_tissues` wrote. Nothing is carried
    when no row was padded, so a complete cohort reaches the objective in the
    form it always did.
    """
    import torch

    from preffect.data.tensors import to_tensors
    from preffect.data.tissues import MultiTissueData, ghost_rows

    parts = [
        to_tensors(t, model_config.correction_variables, with_network=with_network)
        for t in tissues
    ]
    if len(parts) == 1:
        return parts[0]
    ghosts = [ghost_rows(t) for t in tissues]
    if not any(g.any() for g in ghosts):
        return MultiTissueData(parts)
    # copy(), because an annotation read from a file is not writable and
    # torch.from_numpy on a read-only array warns about undefined behaviour.
    return MultiTissueData(parts, ghosts=[torch.from_numpy(g.copy()) for g in ghosts])

def hide_entries(data, fraction: float, seed: int | None):
    """Hide a fraction of the entries at random, keeping the full counts as the targets.

    What ``--hide`` does: the model is shown counts with the hidden entries set
    to zero and scored against the originals, so its error on the hidden
    entries can be reported and watched (``TrainConfig.stop_on``). With a seed
    the same entries are hidden every time.
    """
    from dataclasses import replace

    import numpy as np
    import torch

    from preffect.data.masking import apply_mask, mcar_mask
    from preffect.data.tensors import TensorData
    from preffect.errors import ConfigError

    if not isinstance(data, TensorData):
        raise ConfigError(
            "--hide works for the simple and single models; the full model's data "
            "has one table per tissue, and hiding entries across them is not built"
        )
    counts = data.inputs.detach().cpu().numpy()
    mask = mcar_mask(counts.shape[0], counts.shape[1], fraction, np.random.default_rng(seed))
    shown = torch.from_numpy(apply_mask(counts, mask)).to(data.inputs.dtype)
    # library_scale cleared on purpose, so it is derived from the mask being
    # applied here rather than copied from whatever the data arrived with. A
    # scale given by hand wins over the mask, which is what lets a mini-batch
    # carry one, and it would silently win here too.
    return replace(data, inputs=shown, mask=mask, library_scale=None)

def build_model(kind, n_genes: int, model_config, n_tissues: int):
    """An untrained model of the requested kind."""
    from preffect.config import ModelKind

    if kind is ModelKind.SIMPLE:
        from preffect.model import SimpleModel

        return SimpleModel(n_genes, model_config)
    if kind is ModelKind.SINGLE:
        from preffect.graph_model import SingleModel

        return SingleModel(n_genes, model_config)
    from preffect.full_model import FullModel

    return FullModel(n_genes, model_config, n_tissues=n_tissues)

Say how many edges the network has, not merely that it exists.

Saying "a sample-sample network" was misleading: every dataset version 0.1 shipped carries an identity matrix there, which is a network with no edges at all. Someone reading that line would reasonably fit a graph model and get nothing for ten times the parameters. Findings 35 and 54.

def describe_network(tissue) -> str:
    """Say how many edges the network has, not merely that it exists.

    Saying "a sample-sample network" was misleading: every dataset version 0.1
    shipped carries an identity matrix there, which is a network with no edges
    at all. Someone reading that line would reasonably fit a graph model and
    get nothing for ten times the parameters. Findings 35 and 54.
    """
    import numpy as np

    from preffect.data.graph import ADJACENCY_KEY, has_adjacency

    if not has_adjacency(tissue):
        return "no network"

    matrix = tissue.obsm[ADJACENCY_KEY]
    dense = matrix.toarray() if hasattr(matrix, "toarray") else np.asarray(matrix)
    dense = np.array(dense)
    np.fill_diagonal(dense, 0)
    edges = int(np.count_nonzero(dense))

    if edges == 0:
        return (
            "a network with NO edges between samples, so the graph models "
            "have nothing to use; fit the simple model"
        )
    return f"a network with {edges // 2} edge(s), {edges / tissue.n_obs:.1f} per sample"

def inspect_split(folder: Path, n_tissues: int = 1) -> SplitReport:
    """Read a split and report on it without fitting anything.

    The check the command line's ``check`` makes, as a value rather than as
    printed lines, so the interface can show the same thing. A folder that
    cannot be read at all gives a report with no tissues and the message.
    """
    from preffect.data.checks import check_tissues
    from preffect.data.loading import load_tissues
    from preffect.data.tissues import unmatched_counts
    from preffect.errors import PreffectError

    folder = Path(folder)
    try:
        tissues = load_tissues(folder, n_tissues)
    except PreffectError as error:
        return SplitReport(folder=folder, tissues=(), problem=str(error))
    try:
        unmatched = unmatched_counts(tissues, split=folder.name)
    except PreffectError:
        # A correspondence table that cannot be read at all is reported by
        # check_tissues or by the alignment, with its own message. Counting is
        # the lesser question, so it gives up quietly rather than pre-empting
        # the sentence that says what is actually wrong.
        unmatched = {}
    summaries = tuple(
        TissueSummary(
            samples=t.n_obs,
            genes=t.n_vars,
            network=describe_network(t),
            unmatched=unmatched.get(f"tau_{i}", 0),
        )
        for i, t in enumerate(tissues, start=1)
    )
    try:
        check_tissues(tissues, split=folder.name)
    except PreffectError as error:
        return SplitReport(folder=folder, tissues=summaries, problem=str(error))
    return SplitReport(folder=folder, tissues=summaries)

def apply_checkpoint(
    model_path: Path,
    data_folder: Path,
    *,
    n_tissues: int = 1,
    device="cpu",
    report: Callable[[str], None] | None = None,
):
    """Load a saved model, read a folder of counts, and run the model over it.

    :param n_tissues: how many tissue files the folder holds. Only consulted
        if the model did not record its own count; a model saved by this
        version always does.
    :param device: where to run, as returned by
        :func:`preffect.training.resolve_device`. A string is passed to
        PyTorch as it is; resolve it first if it might name a device the
        machine lacks.
    :param report: called with each progress line; leave unset for silence.
    :returns: the :class:`~preffect.inference.InferenceResult`, the tissues it
        was computed on with their genes already matched to the model's, and
        the checkpoint. Where the full model was given a cohort with patients
        missing the predicted tissue, the rows padded in for them are dropped
        from the result **and** from the first tissue returned, so the two
        still line up row for row.
    """
    from preffect.checkpoint import load_checkpoint
    from preffect.data.selection import GeneSelection, apply_gene_selection
    from preffect.data.tissues import ghost_rows
    from preffect.inference import infer

    def say(line: str) -> None:
        if report is not None:
            report(line)

    data_folder = Path(data_folder)
    checkpoint = load_checkpoint(model_path)
    say(
        f"loaded a {checkpoint.model_config.kind.value} model written by PREFFECT "
        f"{checkpoint.written_by}, applying on {device}"
    )

    n_tissues = int(checkpoint.extra.get("n_tissues", n_tissues))
    kind = checkpoint.model_config.kind
    model = build_model(kind, checkpoint.n_genes, checkpoint.model_config, n_tissues)
    model.load_state_dict(checkpoint.model_state)
    model.to(device)

    tissues = read_split(data_folder, n_tissues)
    if checkpoint.gene_names is not None:
        # Match the genes the model was fitted on, by name. Without this a
        # column could mean a different gene than it did during training,
        # which is finding 18.
        selection = GeneSelection(names=checkpoint.gene_names, basis="from the model")
        tissues = apply_gene_selection(tissues, selection, data_folder.name)
        say(f"matched {len(selection)} genes to the ones the model was fitted on")

    data = to_model_data(tissues, checkpoint.model_config, kind.uses_adjacency).to(device)
    result = infer(model, data)
    if result.n_padded_rows_dropped:
        say(
            f"dropped {result.n_padded_rows_dropped} row(s) that were padded in "
            f"for patients with no sample in the predicted tissue; nothing in "
            f"them was measured"
        )
        real = ~ghost_rows(tissues[0])
        tissues = [tissues[0][real].copy(), *tissues[1:]]
    return result, tissues, checkpoint
